  away by a PREEMPT AND ABORT, by a voluntary REGISTER-with-zero which retires
  nothing, or by nexus-loss cleanup, and READ KEYS cannot tell them apart.

- **The retirement boundary of the shipping target is now MEASURED, and it
  arrives 26 seconds before the witness the code actually keys on.**
  `tests/pr_retirement_probe.sh` is new and makes the measurement entirely from
  the initiators, because the shipping LUN is a closed-source appliance: the
  tree's existing in-flight discriminator holds the victim's write with
  `dm-delay` under the target's backing store and times the PR completion from
  a trace probe inside the target, and neither is available. The victim runs 32
  O_DIRECT threads writing rising counters into 32 blocks; the survivor reads
  that window in a tight loop and logs every change; the victim is
  **power-cut**, not shut down, so whatever it had submitted is left in the
  target's queue with nobody to answer to. Measured (`prret_s75t`): the writer
  was demonstrably reaching the platter (383 change rows, counter 14180), the
  window went quiescent at the cut and **never changed again for 160.3 s**
  (`LATE_ROWS=0`), and READ KEYS went 2,2,1,1,… — the registration purge landed
  between 30 s and 46 s after the cut, about 26 s *after* the platter had
  already gone quiet. The verdict needs no cross-host clock: the survivor
  derives the victim's death from its own readback going quiet. It is a
  qualified contract for one target, firmware, backend and session topology,
  bounded by the observer's 50 ms resolution, and covering nexus loss only —
  never a general property of SPC targets. It is declared, with its evidence,
  at `data/rigs.json` `task_retirement_on_nexus_loss`, and
  `mxfs_rig_retirement_class` in `tests/lib/rig.sh` makes a harness that
  predicts a recovery across a boot boundary ABORT on a rig that declares
  nothing, the same way the registration-purge class already works.

- **The boot-succession certificate says what it depends on.** Its three
  identity conditions plus the registration check are identity and admission;
  the retirement half is a property of the target and is not witnessed by any
  of them. The `P238-FENCE-BOOT-SUCCESSION` line now says so in the evidence
  rather than leaving a reader to infer it, and the function's header records
  what was measured and what would break it. This is why a new ledger record
  was opened against shipped code rather than against new code.

- **The lost-response entry's phase B verdict is inverted, and it gains a phase
  C.** It used to demand a certificate naming the gate within the bound. With
  the victim alive in its original incarnation no retirement proof exists, so
  **blocking is correct and a certificate is the defect** — whichever mechanism
  it names. Liveness is owed from the boot boundary, which supplies admission
  and retirement from one event, and phase C is where it is now required:
  certify by boot succession, replay the slice, let the peer back in.

- **A wedged node in the 2-node fleet was being refused recovery by a guard
  asking the wrong question.** `power_cycle_node` refused whenever
  `MXFS_NODE_LIST` was set, on the reasoning that such nodes are external hosts
  with no libvirt domain — but every 2-node harness sets
  `MXFS_NODE_LIST=test1,test2`, and those *are* domains in this fleet. So a
  wedged `test1` was told "virsh has no domain for them" while `virsh list
  --all` listed it, and the lap was thrown away; that cost two laps in one
  session. The guard now asks what its own comment says it asks — whether a
  libvirt domain of that name answers (`virsh domstate`, bounded, rc 0 for a
  shut-off domain and rc 1 for an unknown one, checked both ways). A real host
  such as a Proxmox node still gets the loud refusal, and so does a libvirtd
  that cannot answer inside the bound, because "cannot establish" has to fail
  closed rather than fall through to a power cycle.

- **A fast non-zero exit is not a fail-fast.** The phase A probe did
  `stat … 2>&1 >/dev/null; echo RC=$?`, keeping one bit. ENOENT is also `rc=1`
  and also instant, and it means the operation never reached the frozen grant
  the check claims to test — measured on lap `s74j`, which returned `rc=1` in
  0 s with the acquire path's abort counter at **zero**, an unfalsifiable pass.
  The probe now runs three targets (the mount root, the directory the victim
  created, and the file its writer is appending to when it is fenced),
  classifies each errno, keeps the verbatim stderr, and requires EIO
  corroborated by the kernel's own abort line. A probe that reaches no frozen
  grant is reported as an ABORT about the harness, never as a FAIL about the
  filesystem.

## 2026-09-19 — 0.89.11 — the instrument is closed: both sides of the 59-entry capture gate are measured, and the fence matrix moves from endpoint cuts to a real command whose evidence is lost

Module srcversion A0C7DCDF168D20DE5C164B1. Two kernel changes: the fence-matrix
lost-response injection (measured on C12E324A74404FFBD800AFF) and the
ambiguous-attempt fail-fast that the injection's first lap exposed. The
capture-gate work below carries no kernel change and was measured on
9DEAC25CCBE89317A188124.

- **The capture-contract instrument is closed on the release configuration.** A
  harness could print FAIL, VACUOUS or PASS about MXFS from a capture nothing
  wrote (the shared ssh helper discarded the remote command's stderr, so a
  failed measurement and a clean system produced the same count), and a second
  producer of the same signature could acquire a well-formed measurement from a
  device belonging to another rig. Both are now measured shut. The capture
  boundary lives in tests/lib/rig.sh: rsx keeps the remote command's status and
  its stderr separately, and capture_require asserts the tool's own required
  structure in the parent shell and ABORTs — never FAILs, never VACUOUS, never
  PASSes — on a capture that observed nothing. The device under test is a
  declared identity: mxfs_dev_resolve takes MXFS_DEV, else the node's own live
  mxfs mount, else the transport default only when the transport is explicit,
  and ABORTs otherwise; data/rigs.json declares the LUN's WWID per rig and every
  lap prints the resolved DEVICE line with its wwid and fsid.
  Fault side 58/58: every entry ABORTed at its injected first measurement with
  no verdict after it. Healthy side 59/59, re-adjudicated this session from the
  stored lap logs rather than from the record's prose — 45 clean PASS, 7 more
  PASS in older verdict formats that a RESULT-token match silently misses,
  d0940_unknown_blocker_probe PASS (below), fence_crash_cuts measured by its own
  sweeps (12/12), 4 entries reporting VACUOUS or INCONCLUSIVE in their own words
  with the unreached precondition named, and d0521's FAIL attributed to its own
  open kernel record. Zero of the 59 harnesses still hardcode another rig's
  device; 32 call the resolver directly.

- **d0940_unknown_blocker_probe measured PASS on the deployed build** (gate
  s74a: RESULT: PASS fails=0 wall=311s, gate rc=0 entries=1 broken=0 vacuous=0
  against a 480 s bound; DEVICE node=test1 path=/dev/sda source=live-mount
  wwid=naa.6e843b6393a5a6ed918bd4f4fdb8e7d6). Its earlier FAIL was the harness,
  not the module: the assertions were written for the pre-0.75.81 import path
  and demanded that an UNKNOWN-owner blocker be installed and re-attributed on
  timeout, while the design has two exits — retired at import as a vacant-slot
  bit, or installed and then dropped by that owner's purge. The join bound was
  also derived before the ghost-window admission hold this probe's
  whole-cluster-crash return now performs. Re-derived from the module's 122 s
  admission bound to 130 s, and the assertions now read: the injection fired
  (vacuity first), retired + dropped + resolved >= injections, every installed
  UNKNOWN blocker dropped or re-attributed with none left standing, both mounts
  complete with no shutdown, and the phantom wait bounded. Measured: injections
  fired, 25 retired at import, zero UNKNOWN blockers left standing, zero phantom
  waits, both mounts clean.

- **A node that could not fence a dead peer hung forever on that peer's grants;
  it now fails those operations and can be torn down.** Refusing to recover a
  slice without proof of exclusion is the invariant and is untouched. Making
  every waiter hang on that refusal was not part of it.
  The acquire path already has the right destination: a slice marked
  RECOVERY_BLOCKED makes operations needing its frozen grants fail fast with EIO
  instead of waiting out an acquire budget. That gate was reachable from exactly
  one place — the pre-command leg's bounded series, through
  `v5_fence_retry_arm(nonproving)`. A fencing attempt that ended AMBIGUOUS (a
  PREEMPT-family command may have reached the target and its outcome was never
  established) disarms the retry instead, so it never reached the gate and its
  waiters were never told anything.
  Measured before, on 2 nodes / TCP: the survivor's own root-inode acquire sat
  behind the fenced victim's EX for 764 s and still climbing, `umount` and
  `fuser` hung on it, the module could not be released, and cluster prep
  reported the node "unusable after power cycle" — with zero BUG, zero Oops and
  zero shutdown. It did not crash; it hung, and only a power cycle cleared it.
  `v5_fence_block_ambiguous()` now marks such a slice RECOVERY_BLOCKED, after the
  disarm and with the slot left unarmed. It certifies nothing, grants nothing and
  clears no durable evidence, and it cannot turn the ambiguous state into a
  retryable one: the retry worker visits only armed slots, and the descriptor
  still carries the "may have run" flag that makes every retry predicate answer
  no. Re-issuing a command against a victim key whose predecessor may still be in
  flight is precisely what the phase distinction exists to prevent.
  Measured after, same reproducer and same rig: the fail-fast fires for the first
  time, a stat that previously retried for 764 s returns EIO in 4 s, and umount
  plus module removal complete cleanly in a 3 s teardown.
  **What this does not fix**, and why the ledger record stays open: the prover
  still cannot resume its own unresolved attempt, so with a valid fresh proof
  available it publishes no certificate, the slice's recovery never completes and
  a returning peer cannot mount. A design consult ruled that path out for now —
  the sole-survivor gate preempts *current* registrants, and the victim is no
  longer one, so the gate does not drain tasks belonging to the already-removed
  registration. That obligation has to be closed before a live prover may certify
  from it.

- **The fence matrix moves past endpoint cuts, and the first new entry found a
  critical stability defect on the release configuration.** The six prover crash
  cuts are measured on both victim arms (12/12), and a design consult ruled what
  comes next (docs/rulings/fence-lost-response-live-prover.md): not another
  crash cut, but a real PREEMPT AND ABORT that *executes* against a
  live-but-silent victim while its successful result is lost on the way back to
  the fencing code — with the prover still alive and still deciding. Cut 4 loses
  the proof *with* the prover and recovers across a boot boundary; this loses
  only the evidence, which is an ordinary transport ambiguity rather than an
  exotic crash.
  The injection is `dbg_prout_lose_key` in pal/linux/kern.c: one-shot, keyed on
  the victim's own PR key, placed after the real completion and before that
  function's own classification, so the substituted -ETIMEDOUT travels exactly
  the path an unanswered command travels (P302-PROUT-ABORT-FAIL included) and
  reaches the caller as kind ERROR at phase MAY_HAVE_SUBMITTED. Placing it after
  the reporting block instead would have returned the right value while omitting
  a log line the real path emits — an observable difference between the injected
  state and the state being modelled. The real result is printed as a witness for
  the test alone; no MXFS path reads it and it is never delivered later.
  tests/fence_lost_response.sh implements the ruling's two-part verdict, because
  "a certificate or a named block" would pass an implementation that always
  blocks.
  **Measured (2/tcp, build C12E324A74404FFBD800AFF): the safety half is correct
  and the liveness half is broken.** The prover published no certificate, did not
  relabel the victim key's absence as PREEMPT_ABORT_DONE nor as
  BOOT_SUCCESSION_ABSENT, kept its durable arm, and stayed alive — all of which
  the lap verified against target-backed PR state rather than log order. But it
  then hung: 23 sweep lines over 683 s saying the attempt is held by "our current
  incarnation ... not taking it over", zero gate attempts, zero certificates,
  while a valid fresh proof was available the whole time (the victim key absent
  and the prover the only live member is precisely the sole-survivor
  exclusive-write gate's precondition). The prover's filesystem blocked on the
  root inode held by the fenced victim for 764 s and climbing, umount hung, and
  only a power cycle cleared it — with zero BUG, zero Oops and zero shutdown, so
  the node does not crash, it hangs.
  That behaviour is the already-filed D-FENCE-POSTSUBMIT-AMBIGUITY-NO-RECONCILIATION-381,
  whose evidence until now was code inspection only and whose reach was recorded
  as 32 nodes from a keyword sweep. It is **2 nodes, measured**, and it hangs a
  node, so it is a gate for the 2-node TCP release rather than a 32-node concern.
  The queue's release view now reports two blockers, both adjudicated from
  evidence and none from a keyword sweep.

## 2026-09-19 — 0.89.7 — the checker's interior btree walk read the child pointers at the wrong byte and judged a clean two-level inobt as corrupt

Patch version: tools/chk_mxfs.c and its harness only; the module is
unchanged (srcversion 9FE0EA9A4DEF0C4700F5A41).

- The defect (ledger D-A-TEST-HARNESS-CAN-REPORT-A-VERDICT-ABOUT-MXFS: a
  verifier's verdict that its instrument did not earn): every interior-node
  walker in chk_mxfs placed a short-format btree block's child pointer array
  at header + numrecs × keylen. XFS places it at header + MAXRECS × keylen
  (xfs_btree_ptr_offset; 505 keys of 4 bytes for the inobt at 4 KiB blocks,
  336 keys of 8 bytes for the bno/cnt trees). The walk therefore read the
  unused key slots, decoded a child agbno of 0, read the AG's block 0 — the
  superblock — and reported "magic expected 0x49414233, got 0x58465342" and
  a CRC failure for each child, then every count derived from the walk was
  wrong (inobt total 0 against an AGI count of 20224, finobt free 17 against
  inobt free 0, filesystem inobt sum 64 against icount 20288). Ten errors
  on a platter both nodes had just unmounted cleanly. No test filesystem
  had ever carried more than one inobt leaf per AG (252 chunk records,
  16128 inodes), so the level-1 arm had never executed.
- Proven on the platter before the patch (test2, direct read of AG 0 block
  2179 = LUN block 113462): magic IAB3, level 1, numrecs 2; keys 128 and
  8832 at byte 56; zeros at byte 64, where the walk looked; pointers 3 and
  2178 at byte 2076, where XFS puts them.
- The fix: sbtree_node_maxrecs/sbtree_ptr_off compute the pointer offset
  from the block size and the key length, and a block whose numrecs exceeds
  maxrecs is an error, at all five walkers — walk_freespace_btree (bno/cnt,
  8-byte keys), walk_inobt (inobt/finobt), orphan_walk_inobt, ds_walk_inobt
  and de_walk_inobt (4-byte keys). The three audit walkers had returned
  silently on the magic mismatch, so on a two-level inobt the orphan audit
  printed "OK (0 allocated inodes ...)" — a vacuous pass — while only the
  dirent walk's own vacuity gate ("no directory was walked") turned it into
  an error. Any earlier chk_mxfs verdict on an AG with more than 16128
  inodes, or more than 505 free extents, was read through this defect.
- tests/chk_mounted_node_reads_platter.sh now asserts the checker's verdict
  on the quiescent platter (rc 0, no ERROR lines), not only its icount: s69a
  PASSed its own assertions while the checker printed ten errors, which is
  exactly the fabricated-verdict class the harness exists for.
- `chk_mxfs --geometry`: the envelope offsets and the XFS geometry, no
  verdict, through a plain read-only open. The 0.89.6 exclusive open refuses
  the full check on a node whose module holds the device, and an inventory
  of the 59 checker call sites in tests/ (s70) found four that only wanted
  agcount/agblocks/inopblog/xfs_data_offset from a live node through `-v`
  and would now parse nothing: tests/tcp_death_replay.sh (W, mounted),
  tests/closure_reuse_directed.sh and tests/closure_footprint_shapes.sh
  (the audit host, test1), tests/typeflip_dead_incarn_repro.sh (the image
  on clyde). Those values are mkfs-time constants — resize_mxfs is their
  only other writer and runs offline under its own exclusive open — so the
  page cache's first image is the current value and the stale-image hazard
  does not apply; the listing says that its counts are the platter's at the
  last unmount. All four now call --geometry. Measured on test1 while
  mounted: --geometry rc 0 with agcount=24 agblocks=541497 agblklog=20
  inopblog=3 xfs_data_offset=455815168; the full check rc 4 with the EBUSY
  text. Of the other mounted-node sites, --pr-keys (2) is a PERSISTENT
  RESERVE IN passthrough and --show-quarantine (1) already reads its
  records O_DIRECT; the seven sess427-439 32/caw chain scripts that grep
  ledger and identity lines from a mounted node's `-v` are now refused
  there, which is the correct answer to a read that was always through the
  page cache — they are not gate entries and do not run on the 2/tcp rig.
- The oracle is now calibrated (ledger
  D-THE-CLUSTERED-STRUCTURAL-AUDIT-GATE-DOES-NOT-ESTABLISH-THAT, item 2):
  tests/chk_oracle_calibration.sh runs on the host alone — a 512 MiB image
  behind a loop device, tools/xfs_block_patch.py setting one big-endian
  field and refreshing the block's XFS CRC so the checker meets a semantic
  inconsistency rather than a checksum failure, the geometry read from the
  clean control's own listing. s70i PASS fails=0 in 78 s
  (tests/evidence/20260919T163021Z_chkcalib_s70i): the fresh format is clean;
  AGI freecount+1, AGI count+64, finobt record freecount-1, the first inode
  chunk's 8 blocks re-listed as free in the bnobt, and sb icount+64 each exit
  4 with their detector's own line (the cross-tree audit names all 8 chunk
  blocks); a missing device, a zeroed sector 0, an image truncated to 1 MiB,
  a 10 ms bound and a SIGSEGV-killed checker are all non-clean (4, 4, 4, 124,
  139) with no verdict printed. Not constructible offline and recorded as
  such in the record: a dinode home aliasing a directory data block (the
  checker has no such detector — a gap, not a fixture) and the two-level
  inobt shape of the defect above.
- Two capture-gate harnesses scored BROKEN for a harness-shape reason:
  tests/d0932_retire_pending_takeover.sh and
  tests/d0932_owner_depart_takeover.sh printed a FAIL line for the
  precondition "the departed prover's/owner's attempt is still standing",
  then declared themselves VACUOUS — and the gate counts VACUOUS only with
  zero FAIL lines. The state is unreachable by design (the clean departure
  waits for the node's own parked recovery work; measured s578j, s53b, s70c),

  verdict. The owner-depart harness's vacuity exit also left the victim VM

- Verified s70a through the capture gate (tests/evidence/
  20260919T154804Z_capture_gate_s70a): fault lap ABORT at the injection with

  inodes / 319 records, filesystem inobt sum 20480 = superblock icount

## 2026-09-19 — 0.89.6 — the offline checker refuses a node whose module holds the device and drops the device's cached pages first; a format or resize on a block device is direct I/O or nothing

Patch version: tools only (tools/chk_mxfs.c, tools/mkfs_mxfs.c,
tools/resize_mxfs.c), one harness, one ruling; the module is unchanged
(srcversion 9FE0EA9A4DEF0C4700F5A41).

- The class (ledger D-A-TEST-HARNESS-CAN-REPORT-A-VERDICT-ABOUT-MXFS,
  measured s67e): the module writes the LUN with bios that never touch the
  block device inode's page cache, and the kernel drops that cache only at
  the device's LAST close. A buffered reader on a node where any opener
  still holds the device — its own mount above all — is served the image
  the first buffered read cached, for as long as the device stays open.
  Every Python and shell instrument moved to O_DIRECT at 0.89.4/0.89.5;
  three C readers remained: chk_mxfs's main check descriptor, and the silent
  non-direct fallbacks in mkfs_mxfs and resize_mxfs.
- Design consult (Astra), banked in
  docs/rulings/checker-page-cache-and-exclusion.md: the check is an offline
  check, so the main descriptor opens O_EXCL and a node whose own mount (or
  a mount in progress) holds the device is refused with EBUSY — a refusal
  is a result, a verdict read through that mount's page cache is not — and
  it drops the device's cached pages (BLKFLSBUF) before its first read, so
  the leftovers of any plain opener on the node are not what it reads. A
  BLKFLSBUF failure aborts the check (it needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN, and a check
  that cannot say what it read is not a check); a regular-file image skips
  it. This is local exclusion only: cluster quiescence stays the caller's
  obligation. A full aligned direct-I/O layer under the checker was not
  taken: its write side is a read-modify-write of enclosing units and is
  only correct under the same offline contract, so it buys nothing here.
- mkfs_mxfs and resize_mxfs: on a block device the direct open succeeds or
  the tool stops. O_SYNC is not O_DIRECT (it changes when a write is
  durable, not what a read returns), and a format verified through a
  buffered descriptor verifies the page cache's copy. The buffered fallback
  survives only for a regular-file image whose filesystem has no direct
  I/O, recognised by the open's own error (EINVAL, EOPNOTSUPP) and
  announced. Resize's discovery read was buffered as well, and fixing only
  the write reopen cannot undo a plan already made from stale geometry, so
  both of its descriptors are direct.
- tests/chk_mounted_node_reads_platter.sh (capture gate entry, 120 s fault
  / 380 s healthy): arm 1, the checker on a mounted node is refused (rc 4,
  the EBUSY text, no superblock line, the node still mounted); arm 2, B
  unmounted with the device held open by a plain sleep, a buffered and a
  direct read of the superblock agree (the seed), A creates 200 files and
  unmounts, the direct read moves and the buffered read does not (the
  hazard is live, or the lap is VACUOUS), then the checker's icount is the
  platter's and a later buffered read on B returns the platter too (the
  invalidation reached every reader on the node). s69a PASS fails=0 in
  58 s: seed 20096/20096, after A's unmount direct 20288 against buffered
  20096, checker 20288, buffered afterwards 20288. The checker's ten errors
  in that lap are the 0.89.7 defect above.
- depart_takeover_unmount (0.89.5's fix) re-lapped s68a PASS 524 s and s68b
  PASS 664 s; its budget row is derived in tests/criteria/TIMEOUT_BUDGETS.md.

## 2026-09-19 — 0.89.5 — the unmount-inside-a-takeover harness builds its authority under grants, so its pass exists on a fresh filesystem

Patch version: harness and manifest only (tests/depart_takeover_unmount.sh,
tests/capture_gate.manifest); the module is unchanged
(srcversion 9FE0EA9A4DEF0C4700F5A41).

- The harness defect (found by the capture-gate lap s67l on 0.89.4,
  tests/evidence/gate_s67l/depart_takeover_unmount.log and test1's kernel
  journal 14:46:20-30Z): the ghost arm let B leave first and then had A,
  alone, create its NFILES files, expecting the lone remount's takeover-only
  pass to spend minutes over those files' ledger pages. A lone mount modifies
  everything at NL with no grant and writes no ledger record, so the
  predecessor incarnation held 10 pages (P-TAUTH-TAKEOVER cand=10,
  pages_prepared=9, total_ms=2714) and the pass was over before the harness's
  first 5 s sample; the lap ABORTed at its own precondition ("the pass was
  not seen in flight", activations=10). The ~15k-page passes the s588 laps
  measured were an aged ledger's residue, which a freshly prepared
  filesystem does not carry.
- The fix: the ghost arm now creates the files while both nodes are members
  (each create takes its inode's grant and the ledger records it, ~14 ms a
  create), then B unmounts and hands the pages it masters to A, then A
  unmounts as the last member and remounts — the ordering
  tests/join_during_takeover.sh has used since s592. The manifest runs it
  with NFILES=8000 (~1000 pages, a ~30 s pass against a ~12 s detection),
  and the harness reports A's activation labels after B's hand-off.

## 2026-09-19 — 0.89.4 — a victim's ledger records are retained on the strength of the platter's recovery descriptor, a format refuses under a live heartbeat writer, and the writer that broke mkfs was a foreign host

Patch version: one predicate in dlm/v5_mount.c (the module's srcversion
moves from 82222A48950939F6D06C57A to 9FE0EA9A4DEF0C4700F5A41), the
rig-side prep guard in tests/setup/prep_fs.sh, and userspace tools and
harnesses; no on-disk or wire change.

- The defect (D-A-MOUNT-S-ORPHAN-SWEEP-RETIRES-THE-LEDGER-RECORDS, high,
  stability, 2/tcp; measured s67f on 0.89.3,
  tests/evidence/20260919T135424Z_d0356spr_s67f-*/B_journal.txt): node A
  declared B dead and wrote a durable FENCING intent into B's slot, its 21
  fence attempts were refused by the harness's injected refusal, and A
  unmounted cleanly, giving the attempt back unowned with the descriptor
  standing at FENCING.  B cold-booted and mounted alone.  Its mount ran the
  orphan sweep before its join gate had declared anything: the sweep's dead
  test (not a slot occupant by the slot-node map, which does not map a
  RECOVERY_GUARD record; not in the view) called B's previous incarnation
  dead, and the 0.89.3 judging predicate — built from this node's own
  recovery-pending marker, which B had not set yet — answered "not
  judging" (P-TAUTH-ORPHAN-AUTH pages=3 dead=1 judging=0).  The sweep took
  the three pages over and retired the victim's records.  Only then did the
  barrier set the marker, take the stranded attempt over, certify by boot
  succession and seal the fence-time manifest — with zero entries
  (P-RMAN-COLLECT-TAUTH entries=0).  The replay judged the slice's one
  transaction (six committed images of an inode-chunk create and directory
  blocks in AG 1) as not held (P273-SHADOW-EVAL notheld=6,
  P-ICREATE-AUTH verdict=REFUSE why=ag-sibling-refused), skipped it
  atomically, refused the slice (-117, P227-FR-TORN-UNPUBLISHED) and
  quarantined AGs 0-1 cluster-wide (P241-RECOV-TERMINAL ag_mask=0x3).  B's
  mount completed but every read in the domain was EIO and A's rejoin
  failed at AG 0 (mount rc 32).  The 0.89.3 rationale, that the victim's
  frozen ACTIVE record keeps it the occupant of its slot until the death is
  declared, does not hold once a prover has converted the slot to a
  descriptor and departed.
- dlm/v5_mount.c v5_recovery_judging_cb: the local marker is a hint, the
  platter is the authority.  With no marker naming {node, inc} the
  predicate reads the 64 slot records: an ACTIVE record naming that
  incarnation contradicts the caller's "dead" and protects
  (P-TAUTH-RETENTION-ACTIVE); a RECOVERY_GUARD whose descriptor names it
  as the victim below IMAGES_REPLAYED protects at any owner, lease state or
  age (P-TAUTH-RETENTION-PLATTER) — a descriptor nobody advances protects
  the records for as long as it stands, which is the fail-closed outcome,
  since the alternative is a manifest sealed against retired records; a
  slot that cannot be read or a descriptor present but undecodable is
  UNKNOWN and protects (P-TAUTH-RETENTION-UNKNOWN), because "no valid
  descriptor found" is evidence only when every slot was classified; an
  unknown incarnation (inc 0) protects.  One completed descriptor is a
  negative only because a victim's descriptor lives in its own slot; the
  scan runs to the end so that a second, unresolved one wins.  The sweep's
  pre-filter and the takeover choke point (dlm_takeover_page) use the same
  callback, so on-demand takeovers obey it too.  Design consult (Astra,
  2026-09-19): the retention obligation is durable and belongs to the
  victim, whoever created it and whoever holds or abandoned the attempt; a
  clean departure ends the prover's participation, not the victim's
  recovery obligation; retention is a different question from liveness, so
  it stays in the reclamation predicate rather than in the occupancy map.
  The consult's further shape — run the mount-time sweep only after the
  mount's recovery census, and make the ACTIVE→GUARD→released handoff an
  explicit invariant — is recorded on the queue record as the next
  obligation; this version ships the one change the measured chain needed.
  Design: docs/tcp-authority-ledger.md, "Dead is not reclaimable".
- Verified s67h on module 9FE0EA9A (tests/evidence/20260919T141542Z_d0356spr_s67h-*,
  2 nodes / TCP, the same harness through the capture gate, 442 s): B's
  sweep logged P-TAUTH-RETENTION-PLATTER node=958260660 slot=1 stage=1
  owner=0 and P-TAUTH-ORPHAN-AUTH pages=2 dead=1 judging=1, took nothing
  over (cand=0); the attempt takeover, the boot-succession certificate and
  the manifest followed with the victim's records in it
  (P-RMAN-COLLECT-TAUTH entries=3 ex=3, P-RMAN-SEALED entries=3); the
  replay of the six images completed, P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE slot=1, the
  barrier admitted with replayed=1 published=0x2 and nothing quarantined;
  B mounted in 28.6 s and read both witnesses, A rejoined in 2.7 s and
  read both; no BUG, Oops or WARNING.  Regression on the same build:
  tests/d0981_pending_victim_sweep.sh s67i PASS 307 s and
  tests/sole_survivor_gate_probe.sh s67j PASS 340 s.  Two of the lap's
  assertions still failed because they demanded that B fence and recover
  the cleanly departed A — the stranded-owner shape from before the
  relinquish-on-departure design, which the harness's own branch already
  notes is not produced; they now follow the measured shape: no fence of
  A, A settled by the peer's PR-key retirement proof
  (P304-RETIRE-COMPLETED-BY-PEER), A's slot EMPTY after B's return.
- The remaining buffered platter readers from 0.89.4's list are converted:
  tools/tauth_page_auth.py reads the ledger region through an O_DIRECT
  reader (4 KiB pages, page-aligned offsets); tests/mxfs_sb_bytecmp.sh's

  tests/hb_live_count.sh's envelope-header read stays buffered and says

  device is open, so the cache cannot hold a stale value of it.  Still
  open: chk_mxfs's main check descriptor (its heartbeat paths already use

## 2026-09-19 — 0.89.3 — a dead authority whose slice replay is still judging its records is not reclaimable

Patch version: a guard at the ledger-page takeover choke point and a
pre-filter in the orphan sweep; no on-disk or wire change (a new test-only
module parameter).

- The defect (D-ORPHAN-SWEEP-RETIRES-A-PENDING-VICTIM-UNDER-REPLAY-0981,
  high, stability, 2/tcp; measured s66e on 0.89.2,
  tests/evidence/20260919T123058Z_d0980_s66e/K_journal.txt): a node
  mounting onto a LUN that carried a certified but unowned recovery
  descriptor (stage FENCED, owner 0 — what a prover leaves when it seals a
  victim's fence and its own mount is then refused at the admission bound)
  declared the victim dead (P163-RECOVERY-PENDING, "purge deferred until
  slice replay completes"), claimed the lease in its first barrier round and
  started the slice stability proof; two seconds later its own departure
  worker's orphan sweep found the victim's ledger pages under a dead
  authority — dead by the sweep's test: not the occupant of any heartbeat
  slot and not in the membership view — took them over and retired the
  victim's records (P-TAUTH-TAKEOVER-RETIRE page=15268 cleared=1
  via=orphan-sweep); the replay's current-safety check then found the sealed
  manifest's entry gone from the live ledger (P-RMAN-POSTSEAL-MUTATION
  live{rc=-2}), aborted -117 and published a terminal whole-filesystem
  quarantine (P-RMAN-MUTATED-TERMINAL), and the next two mounts were refused
  in 22 and 28 ms.  The purge deferral lived on the disklock purge path; the
  sweep was a second retirement path that never asked.  Every earlier lap
  had started from the capture gate's reformat, which is why a LUN in this
  state had never been mounted.
- dlm/dlm.h, dlm/dlm.c, dlm/v5_mount.c: a `recovery_judging_cb` on the DLM
  context — is {node, incarnation} a recovery victim whose slice replay has
  not reached IMAGES_REPLAYED?  The v5 answer is this node's recovery-pending
  marker (set when the death is declared or a peer's fence is seen, which is
  before any dead test can pass, because until then the frozen record keeps
  the victim the occupant of its slot) plus one descriptor read: at
  IMAGES_REPLAYED or beyond the judgement is over and the completion ladder's
  own purge and takeover run as before; a lower stage, an unreadable
  descriptor or a mismatched victim tuple keeps the protection; incarnation
  0 protects.  It is judged at the one choke point every takeover path
  shares, dlm_takeover_page, before the prepare, the activation and the
  purge (P-TAUTH-TAKEOVER-UNDER-JUDGEMENT, -EAGAIN), so the orphan sweep, an
  on-demand takeover for a request that needs the page and the named passes
  all obey it; the sweep pre-filters (P-TAUTH-ORPHAN-AUTH judging=,
  P-TAUTH-ORPHAN-SWEEP judging_pages=) so it does not issue a refused
  takeover per page.  Design consult (Astra, 2026-09-19) set the shape: dead
  is not reclaimable; the protection interval is "pending and below
  IMAGES_REPLAYED" (an "until complete" predicate would refuse the legitimate
  completion takeover, which runs after that stage and before the slot is
  zeroed); enforce at the destructive choke point, pre-filter for
  diagnostics; refusing on-demand takeovers is safe for liveness because a
  request on such a victim's resources is already parked by the
  recovery-blocked cutoff; never weaken the verdict for a local mutator,
  since an absent record cannot say whether a foreign post-seal write landed.
  Design: docs/tcp-authority-ledger.md, "Dead is not reclaimable".
- Verified s66i on 0.89.3
  (tests/evidence/20260919T131428Z_d0981_s66i-*, 2 nodes / TCP, 258 s, every
  assertion PASS; tests/d0981_pending_victim_sweep.sh through the capture
  gate).  test1 built the precondition under the new one-shot test knob
  mxfs.dbg_barrier_refuse_after_claim=1 (the barrier refuses the mount right
  after it claims a slice's recovery lease and gives the lease back durably
  through mxfs_v5_dlm_recovery_relinquish): refused at 71 s with
  P-DBG-BARRIER-REFUSE-AFTER-CLAIM slot=0 relinquish_rc=0, leaving the
  platter with two FENCED descriptors at owner 0/0.  test2 then mounted in
  14 s: its sweep met both victims and left them alone (P-TAUTH-ORPHAN-AUTH
  judging=1 twice, sweep cand=0 judging_pages=6), the first victim's replay
  evaluated its manifest with postseal_mutations=0 and advanced 3->4 at :36,
  the takeover retired its records only afterwards (:38, cleared=1 on page
  20408), P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE for both slots, barrier admitted at
  wait_ms=12911, no quarantine; test1 mounted beside it in 2.8 s; no
  descriptor left on the platter; zero splats.  s66j, the sole-survivor
  probe on 0.89.3: PASS in 324 s (B completed at 155 s, A refused at
  wait_ms=122028 against 122000).  Record removed as FIXED AND VERIFIED.
- Open, not this fix: the verdict path still publishes a terminal
  whole-filesystem quarantine on any post-seal mismatch; the consult
  distinguished "safety could not be established" from "corruption proved"
  and both fail closed, so no change was made there.

## 2026-09-19 — 0.89.2 — the mount admission barrier is bounded by elapsed time and can be ended by a signal

Patch version: a fix inside the mount-path admission barrier and the two
disklock takeover primitives; no on-disk or wire change.

- The defect (D-A-JOINERS-MOUNT-OUTLIVED-ITS-OWN-TIMEOUT-BY-MORE-THAN-A-
  MINUTE-IN-THE-SOLE-SURVIVOR-GATE-PROBE-0980, high, stability, 2/tcp): in
  one lap of tests/sole_survivor_gate_probe.sh on 0.89.1 (s65f) the joiner's
  `timeout 300 mount` had not returned 360 s after it started and ignored
  SIGTERM for all of that; the lap's kernel log was lost.  Four re-laps on
  0.89.1 (s66a-d) all showed the refused-at-30-s shape instead, so the
  overrun was not reproduced; what the code and the s65g journal establish
  is the class.  mxfs_dlm_mount_recovery_barrier bounded its admission wait
  by SUMMING its own 1 s poll sleeps, and every poll pass fell through into
  a replay round whose work the sum never saw: the 6 s abandonment
  observation inside each recovery or fence-attempt takeover (s65g: takeover
  at :03, the new attempt at :10), the slice stability proof of up to 45 s,
  the replay, the ledger takeover scan.  Under the ghost extension that is
  122 polls times whatever a round cost, unbounded in principle.  And nothing
  in the loop looked at signals; msleep is uninterruptible, so a `timeout`
  could only wait for mount(2) to return on its own.  The same class was
  fixed once already for the root inode read (0.75.72); the barrier beside
  it kept the old shape.  A scan of the other eleven loops in the tree that
  advance a counter by their sleep length found the two on the mount path
  (DLM init's peer wait, 15 s, and the stale-slot window, 5 s) doing only
  sector reads in their bodies; the rest run on workers or lock paths.
- xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c: the wait is bounded by a jiffies deadline from the
  loop's start.  It is judged before a round starts (the four inline rounds
  included), before every slice inside a round and after every poll sleep —
  the recovery-safe boundaries, where no lease is being claimed and no slice
  is mid-replay.  A deadline cannot preempt a slice already being replayed,
  so the guaranteed property is that no new work starts past the bound, and
  every exit prints P-BARRIER-CLOCK (wait_ms, bound_ms, overrun_ms, rounds,
  last_round_ms, total_ms): an overrun larger than the last round is a
  defect.  The poll is schedule_timeout_killable, clipped to what remains of
  the bound; a fatal signal at any of those boundaries refuses the mount
  with -EINTR (P-BARRIER-CANCELLED), never -EBUSY, since cancellation is not
  contention; the bound still refuses -EBUSY.  The ghost extension (30 + 62
  + 30 s) is applied once, as a cap, from the loop's start, and kept after
  every death is declared so the replay that becomes possible then has its
  allowance.  The acquire is told what remains of the bound
  (mxfs_v5_dlm_recovery_acquire_bounded): a takeover whose 6 s observation
  plus its 3 s continuation (the CAS, the new PREEMPT AND ABORT, its
  certification and seal — 2 s measured) would not fit is refused up front
  (P238-TAKEOVER-NOBUDGET) instead of run.  dlm/disklock.c: the two
  abandonment waits are interruptible but never shortened — an early wake
  re-sleeps until the full interval has elapsed on the monotonic clock — and
  a fatal signal abandons the observation with -EINTR, taking nothing over.
  Design consult (Astra, 2026-09-19) concurred and set the shape: an
  absolute deadline with cancellation at recovery-safe boundaries, budget
  exhaustion an availability refusal rather than permission to admit, the
  extension a cap, the observation refused when it cannot fit.  Design:
  docs/rulings/mount-admission-barrier.md, "The bound is elapsed time, and
  the wait is cancellable".
- Verified s66g on 0.89.2 (tests/evidence/20260919T124418Z_d0980_s66g-*,
  2 nodes / TCP, 282 s, every assertion PASS; tests/d0980_barrier_killable.sh
  through the capture gate).  K: both VMs destroyed with their mounts in
  flight, test2 mounts under `timeout -s TERM 20`; its barrier is holding on
  two frozen records (P-BARRIER-GHOST-EXTEND undeclared=2 bound_ms=122000)
  when the signal lands at 20 s; the mount returns 376 ms later (MOUNT_RC=124,
  WALL_MS=20376), P-BARRIER-CANCELLED after 9288 ms of the wait,
  P-BARRIER-CLOCK result=cancelled wait_ms=10075 overrun_ms=0, nothing
  admitted, no mount task left, not mounted.  C: test1 then mounts with no
  signal and completes in 88 s (barrier wait 80623 ms of the 122000 bound,
  overrun 0, replayed=2 published=0x3): the cancelled mount left the slices
  where the next owner found them.  R: test2 mounts again in 2.8 s.  Zero
  splats.  s66f, the sole-survivor probe on 0.89.2: PASS in 311 s; the
  joiner refused at wait_ms=30053 against 30000 (32 rounds) and the prover
  at wait_ms=122200 against 122000 (115 rounds), where 0.89.1 took 137-154 s
  of wall for the same 122 s bound.  Record removed as FIXED AND VERIFIED.
- Found by the first, ungated lap of the new harness (s66e) and ledgered as
  D-ORPHAN-SWEEP-RETIRES-A-PENDING-VICTIM-UNDER-REPLAY-0981 (high, stability,
  2/tcp): a mount onto a LUN carrying a certified but unowned recovery
  descriptor claims it, its own orphan sweep retires the victim's ledger
  record during the stability proof, and the replay publishes a
  whole-filesystem quarantine that refuses every later mount.
- tests/d0980_barrier_killable.sh (new; manifest and budget rows added):
  the kill arm, the control mount's overrun against its last round, and the
  retry after cancellation; it exits VACUOUS unless the platter carries
  frozen real-incarnation records and no recovery descriptor.

## 2026-09-19 — 0.89.1 — the re-affirmed grant carries the open-holder snapshot, and a fresh open on a reused number is not poisoned as an old descriptor

Patch version: two fixes inside the 0.89.0 registry, no on-disk or wire
format change (the LOCK_GRANT field already existed; it is now filled on
every path).

- The defect (D-TCP-NO-OPEN-TRACKING-PEER-HELD-FD-READS-THE-REUSED-INODES-NEW-
  FILE-BYTES-0977, critical, integrity, 2/tcp) was still measured on 0.89.0:
  the number was reused under the peer's two descriptors (s64a,
  tests/evidence/20260919T050109Z_d0977).  The instruments placed for it
  showed the grantee receiving the mask on its EX grant (P74-GRANT gen 17
  oh=0x2) and then an EX re-grant of the same durable grant id with oh=0x0
  (gen 18, prov=0), which the guard read (P87-OPEN-CHECK open_holders=0x0) —
  while the master's ledger still carried 0x2 in every later commit.  The
  master's own P-DGEX line (active_b4=1, handoff=0, gen=18) named the path:
  the REAFFIRM arm of process_remote_request, which answers the idempotent
  certify re-acquire every unlink's inactivation makes.  That arm built the
  grant identity field by field and never assigned the 0.89.0 mask field, so
  the re-affirm delivered an unassigned (zero) mask, and the grantee's mirror
  update adopted any exclusive grant's mask unconditionally.  Deterministic:
  every unlink on TCP takes that path.
- dlm/dlm.c: the re-affirm sends the chain entry's mask (stamped from the
  record at the commit); the takeover import (dlm_import_holder) stamps the
  imported record's mask on the entry it installs, so a re-affirm the new
  master later sends names the same snapshot the old master granted; the
  grantee replaces its snapshot only for a grant naming a NEW durable grant id
  (a fresh commit) and ORs a same-id re-affirm's mask into the one it has —
  no peer can publish a mark while the EX is held, so a bit the mirror has and
  a re-affirm lacks is a lost bit, never a cleared one.  Design consult
  (Astra, 2026-09-19) concurred and named the hazards: every chain-
  construction path must carry the mask, OR only within one certificate,
  replace on a fresh commit so fenced peers' bits cannot pin reclamation.
  Design: docs/tcp-authority-ledger.md, "Every path that constructs a grant
  carries the snapshot".
- The second defect (D-A-FRESH-OPEN-ON-A-NUMBER-THE-PEER-REUSED-IS-POISONED-
  AS-A-DESCRIPTOR-OF-THE-OLD-INCARNATION-0979, major, 2/tcp), a regression
  0.89.0's containment introduced and the first verification lap found (s65b,
  tests/evidence/20260919T052148Z_d0977, arm C: B's open of a new file on a
  number it still cached under the previous incarnation succeeded and its
  first read failed; P977-RELOAD-EXPOSED-MISMATCH opens=2 were the open's
  own two descriptors).  xfs_file_open counts the open into i_mxfs_open_n
  BEFORE its protecting acquire, and the reload that runs under that acquire
  read the count as exposure of the old incarnation.  Now the opens still
  inside their acquire are counted separately (i_mxfs_open_inflight, raised
  before the count) and the two poison tests (the reload's generation
  mismatch, the evict ring's freed incarnation) use mxfs_inode_exposed():
  usable descriptors or live mappings only.  The mark-publication tests keep
  counting in-flight opens, which a release must still protect.
- Verified s65c on 0.89.1 (tests/evidence/20260919T053435Z_d0977, 2 nodes /
  TCP, 82 s, every assertion PASS): arm A — the number is not reused under
  B's two descriptors, B's held-fd read returns the original 4096 'V', B's
  write through the held fd reads back, one close keeps the defer, the last
  close is followed by the reap and reuse at 30 s, 75 successor files intact;
  arm B — three victims, two mastered locally and one by the peer, all
  deferred (the remotely mastered one's P74-GRANT shows the fresh commit and
  the re-affirm both carrying 0x2 in s65b); arm D — A reuses the last
  victim's number after B's close, B's fresh open reads the new file's 4096
  'G' with rc 0 and no poison line; arm C — with the registry off the held
  descriptor's read and write refuse ESTALE and the poison line shows
  inflight=0.  Zero splats on both nodes.  The fence-strip face, s65d
  (tests/evidence/20260919T053707Z_d0977death, tests/d0977_opener_death.sh):
  B destroyed while holding the unlinked file's descriptor, A's guard deferred
  three times on B's mark, recovery completed in 52 s, the number was reused
  5 s after the purge, 30 successor files intact, no shutdown, and B rebooted,
  re-prepped and read A's post-fence write.
- tests/d0977_open_unlink_tcp.sh gained arm B (the master is read from the
  kernel ring: the node carrying the victim's P977-REL-MARK op=1 line) and
  arm D; the P977-REL-MARK instrument prints only when a mark is set, kept
  or erased, not on the ordinary clear of an unmarked record.
- tests/sole_survivor_gate_probe.sh: the journals, the platter and any running
  mount's kernel stack are captured before the joins are judged (its s65f
  lap aborted with B's mount outliving its timeout and nothing captured — now
  D-0980), and two assertions are corrected against the inline-replay
  admission rule: an ISSUE is the defect only while another registrant exists
  (s62e's single ISSUE came after B had unregistered and named 0 other
  registrants), and B's mount completes or is refused by the admission bound,
  never hangs.  PASS s65g on 0.89.1 (332 s): B's mount completed in 164 s
  after A's refused mount unregistered, seven gate attempts all refused
  while B was registered.

## 2026-09-19 — 0.89.0 — open-holder marks on the TCP authority ledger: a peer's open file survives an unlink on another node

Minor version: the authority ledger record gains an open-holder mask (ledger
version 4, byte 104 of the entry, where version 3 kept a forensic wall clock),
the LOCK_RELEASE carries the releaser's mark change and the LOCK_GRANT reply
carries the record's mask, so protocol generation 21 excludes every older node
cluster-wide and every volume is re-formatted (prep does it).

- The defect (D-TCP-NO-OPEN-TRACKING-PEER-HELD-FD-READS-THE-REUSED-INODES-NEW-
  FILE-BYTES-0977, critical, integrity, 2/tcp): the cross-node open-unlink
  registry existed only on the CAW slot.  On TCP the release dropped the open
  bit, the holders query returned -EOPNOTSUPP and the destructive-inactivation
  guard treated that as "nobody has it open" and freed; measured s62d on
  0.88.0, the unlinked inode's number was reused under the peer's held
  descriptor and the descriptor read the successor file's 4096 'G' with rc 0.
- The mark lives in the resource's ledger record and moves only inside a
  release transition: a node releasing its grant on an inode publishes its
  ABSOLUTE protected state (open descriptors or live mappings ⇒ set, else
  clear) as the release's open_op, the master applies it in the transition that
  retires the grant, and the ACK follows the commit.  A refused release applies
  no mark and is re-sent; a stale one applies nothing.  The genuine free's
  release erases every node's mark (the guard under that EX proved no occupied
  slot holds the incarnation open).
- The exclusive grant carries the snapshot: the master stamps the record's mask
  on the LOCK_GRANT and the grantee keeps it on its mirror entry, where the
  guard reads it under the held EX with no round trip.  A mark in a heartbeat
  slot the disklock table shows unoccupied is residue and is ignored; a mark in
  an occupied slot is honoured whoever the occupant is, until the owner's fence
  purge strips it at recovery completion.  A guard that defers releases the EX,
  so the reaper's retry (5 s, then every 30 s) takes a fresh grant whose
  snapshot can have seen the last close.
- A mark is cleared only by a release: the last close at NL takes a PR grant
  through the ordinary acquire and its demote publishes the clear; there is no
  standalone clear on the wire.  A FREE tombstone still carrying marks is never
  reclaimed for another resource, which pins one of its home page's entries
  until the last opener clears — the registry's capacity bound, counted as
  open_pinned when a page refuses a grant.
- The guard's -EOPNOTSUPP verdict is now a defer, never a proceed; the only
  registry-less configuration left, a cluster-routed inode on TCP, is refused
  at mount.
- Containment, for what a lost mark degrades to: an exposed shell's incarnation
  is immutable.  When a coherency reload finds the platter naming another
  incarnation while the shell has descriptors or mappings, the shell is
  poisoned — every file operation refuses -ESTALE, faults SIGBUS, the
  revocation worker drops its page cache — instead of adopting the successor's
  forks, and every data path re-checks the poison after its I/O-lock ride,
  where the reload runs.  Measured s64a: with the registry switched off the
  held descriptor's read and write both refused with ESTALE and the successor
  files were intact.
- tests/d0977_open_unlink_tcp.sh (arm A: the registry, multi-opener, last-close
  reap; arm C: the containment with the registry off) and
  tests/d0977_opener_death.sh.  Design: docs/tcp-authority-ledger.md,
  "Open-holder marks".

## 2026-09-19 — 0.88.1 — chk_mxfs walks every directory's entries and names one that points at a free inode

Patch version: a checker pass, no on-disk or protocol change.

- The defect (D-CHK-MXFS-DOES-NOT-WALK-DIRECTORY-ENTRIES-SO-A-DIRENT-NAMING-A-
  FREE-INODE-PASSES-CLEAN-0964, verification, on the 2/tcp release list):
  tools/chk_mxfs parsed no directory name at all — its only directory pass
  was the sharding-manifest scan — so a published dirent naming a freed inode,
  the durable outcome of D-0963 (lists on every node, resolves on none, rm
  cannot remove it), reported CLEAN (tests/evidence/chk_dangling_s605h.log:
  rc 4 for the live ifree lag only, nothing about any directory).  The board's
  chk_clean row could not catch the damage class it exists for.
- tools/chk_mxfs.c: `check_dirents` (step 7d, after the sharding pass).  The
  allocated set is built from the inobt leaf records the inode-btree pass
  validated (a holemask bit per four inodes, a free-mask bit per inode) and
  every directory found there is walked: shortform in the literal area (the
  parent is its '..'; a non-zero i8count widens every number including the
  parent; the entries must end exactly at di_size), and the data blocks of
  block, leaf and node directories through the data fork's extents or its
  bmbt (bmdr root, BMA3 blocks, the pointer array based at capacity), each
  directory block assembled through the sorted extent map, its magic, CRC,
  uuid and owner checked, XDB3 data bounded by the tail's leaf count, every
  record and unused span tagged back to itself and the records partitioning
  the data area exactly.  Each entry's number must be in the allocated set
  AND name a valid v3 dinode for that number (magic, version, di_ino, CRC)
  with a non-zero mode; '.' must be the directory and '..' a directory; an
  ftype contradicting the dinode's class is an error.  The pass prints its
  counts (`dirs= entries= blocks= dangling= mode0= ftype_mismatch= bad_blocks=
  dirs_skipped= allocated=`) and one line per directory under -v; zero
  directories or a root never walked is an error, and every skipped
  directory or unwalkable block is an error, so nothing skipped can read as
  CLEAN.  The design consult (Astra, 2026-09-19) ruled the inobt the
  allocation authority with the dinode a separate validity check (freed
  inode bytes are not erased, so "inobt free, dinode convincing" is still
  dangling), and ruled report-only under -a: removing a name must maintain
  the bestfree table, the hash index and the free index, and it destroys the
  evidence the pass exists to surface.  A live LUN's dirent, inobt and dinode
  can come from different moments — the same caveat as the counters — and the
  offline rows are the authoritative ones.
- tests/d0964_chk_dangling_dirent.sh: four directories in each on-disk format
  (shortform 3, block 100, leaf 300, node 1500 names), both nodes unmounted,
  chk_mxfs -v offline must count exactly the names created plus the dots per
  directory and report the volume clean; then the D-0963 control arm
  (tests/d0963_sf_lagging_flush.sh MODE=control) publishes its dangling entry,
  both nodes unmount, and the checker must name that directory and that name
  with rc 4, retain it under -a, and name it again afterwards.  Gate manifest
  entry (the lap leaves the fleet unmounted; prep after it) and the budget
  table row.
- VERIFIED s62c on the 2/tcp rig (module 9A5DB6C72979614DBF845A6, tools
  0.88.1; tests/evidence/20260919T035557Z_capture_gate_s62c): the fault lap
  ABORTed at its first measurement with no verdict after it; the healthy lap
  PASSed in 103 s of its 300 s bound — offline, the walk counted 4, 102, 302
  and 1502 entries over 1, 2 and 7 blocks for the four fixtures (1917
  entries, 10 blocks, 1911 allocated inodes, dangling 0, rc 0), and after
  the control arm published its entry the checker reported `directory 2168:
  entry 'nodeB_file58' names inode 8388795 which the inobt holds FREE
  (dangling entry)` with rc 4, kept it under -a, and named it again on the
  next plain run.  The same volume reported CLEAN before this pass existed.
- Healthy gate laps re-run for the harness-capture records (s62a, s62d): nine
  short entries.  Three harness instruments were wrong and are fixed:
  tests/rejoin_residue.sh reads the node id from the kernel ring, not
  `journalctl -k` (journald drops kmsg behind the module's print rate; the
  DLM init line was absent there and present in dmesg); tests/d512_t2_pause.sh
  runs its T6 rider after the whole drain-pause ladder (each stage's create
  reused the inode the previous stage's rider had freed, and the peer's
  pending request re-fired a release under the freshly armed pause — the
  "stage 5 leaked" FAIL had existed since 2026-08-24; every stage now holds
  ~3.5 s of a 3 s pause); tests/d512_race_verify.sh drops the page cache
  before its mmap racer (a cached folio is mapped by fault-around and never
  enters xfs_filemap_fault, so the site=fault window could not fire).
  tests/d512_t1_reuse.sh now digests the bytes its held-fd read returns, and
  that measurement found a kernel defect: on the TCP transport the unlinked
  file's inode number was reused under the peer's open descriptor and the
  descriptor read the successor file's 4096 'G' with rc 0 — filed as
  D-TCP-NO-OPEN-TRACKING-PEER-HELD-FD-READS-THE-REUSED-INODES-NEW-FILE-BYTES-
  0977 (critical, integrity, 2/tcp): the open-holder registry exists only on
  the CAW slot, the TCP unlock drops the open bit and the B6 guard proceeds
  on -EOPNOTSUPP.

## 2026-09-19 — 0.88.0 — a slice's payload is zeroed through the kernel FUA path at the slot claim, under a durable per-slice lifecycle record, before the first journal write

Minor version: a new on-disk envelope region and protocol generation 20, so
every volume is re-formatted (prep does it) and a gen-19 node cannot join.

- The defect (D-SLICE-CLAIM-TIME-INIT-UNTRUSTED-ZERO-531, integrity, 2/tcp):
  mkfs zeroes the log region through a userspace write whose durability the
  target stack does not promise, and nothing at claim time re-established a
  known-zero payload.  Measured s60j on 0.87.23: a slice carrying a previous
  incarnation's CRC-valid records beyond a zero block 0 mounted clean, took a
  committed log-forced transaction (mkdir + 40 files), and after the node's
  crash the slice could not be recovered at all — head discovery is
  cycle-number based and per-record uuid validation runs only on the head it
  picks, so it landed on a stale header, `xlog_header_check_mount` refused
  the slice (-117), the node could not mount, and 0 of 40 files came back
  against the control's 40 of 40.  Design consult (Astra, in
  docs/rulings/twin-hole-fix-zeroing-strictness.md) rejected a recovery-side
  uuid mask with a wrapped-log counterexample (masked cycle stamps can make a
  dirty log read as totally zeroed and skip required replay silently) and
  ruled the durable claim-time initialisation, which this release implements.
- include/mxfs/mxfs_super.h: `MXFS_FORMAT_F_SLIFE` and the SLICE LIFECYCLE
  region — `slife_offset`/`slife_size` in the envelope super, 32 KiB laid
  out after the bootstrap region, one 512 B `struct mxfs_slife_record` per
  log slice (magic, version, crc, state INIT_REQUIRED|ZEROING|READY, slice,
  generation, fs_uuid, owner node/epoch, clock).  `MXFS_PROTO_GEN` 20: a
  gen-19 node would mount its slice without the claim-time zero and journal
  into a payload the record still calls untrusted.
- dlm/bootstrap.c, dlm/bootstrap.h: `mxfs_slife_read` validates a record
  (magic, version, slice index, state range, crc, this volume's uuid; a zero
  sector is UNFORMATTED and fails closed) and `mxfs_slife_claim_init` is the
  claimant's state machine: READY returns at once; otherwise ZEROING is
  written FUA and read back, the whole payload is zeroed through
  `mxfs_pal_bdev_write_fua` in 64 KiB chunks, the device is flushed, every
  byte is read back through the FUA read path and compared, and only then is
  READY written FUA and read back with the generation bumped.  Any failure
  leaves the record ZEROING for the slot's next claimant to restart the full
  zero; nothing is ever inferred.  The chunk is 64 KiB of kmalloc memory
  because the readback is a SCSI READ(16) passthrough, which the block layer
  refuses above the LUN's 512 KiB hardware transfer limit and which maps
  pages by virtual address.
- dlm/v5_mount.c, dlm/v5_mount.h: the region is carried in the DLM options
  and context; `mxfs_v5_dlm_slice_lifecycle_claim` supplies the device, the
  volume uuid and the claimant's node/epoch, and
  `mxfs_v5_dlm_slice_lifecycle_state` reads a slice's state for recovery.
  -ENODEV means the volume carries no region.
- pal/linux/xfs_super.c, xfs/xfs_mount.h: the super's region fields are
  validated (holds every slice's record, sector aligned, ends before the XFS
  data) and copied to the mount; after the heartbeat slot claim and before
  `xfs_mountfs` the claimed slot's slice is brought to READY (`P-SLIFE
  before= after= zeroed_bytes= zero_ms=`).  The slice's byte range is
  derived from the superblock's own fields (agno, agbno, blocklog): the
  daddr macros shift by `m_blkbb_log`, which `xfs_sb_mount_common` sets
  only inside `xfs_mountfs`, so before it they return blocks where they
  promise sectors — the first lap of this change (s61a) reported READY
  after zeroing 64 MiB of the data area 23 GiB below the slice, and the
  plant survived untouched.  A slice that does not lie inside the internal
  log refuses the mount (`P-SLIFE-GEOM`).  A refusal is a refused mount
  (`P-SLIFE-REFUSED`); a volume without the region mounts as before, loudly
  (`P-SLIFE-LEGACY`) — nothing synthesises INIT_REQUIRED for a slice that
  may have been used.
- xfs/xfs_log.c: a foreign-slice recovery of a slice whose record is not
  READY replays nothing (`P-SLIFE-FOREIGN-UNINIT`): READY is durable before
  the first journal write, so no record of this incarnation can be in it,
  and its payload is exactly the untrusted bytes the record keeps discovery
  away from; the record is left for the slot's next claimant.  A record that
  cannot be validated is a plain retryable error (`P-SLIFE-FOREIGN-UNREADABLE`).
- tools/mkfs_mxfs.c: lays out the region after the bootstrap record, zeroes
  it, and once the native format has settled the slice count writes one
  INIT_REQUIRED record per slice bound to the new uuid; sets the flag and
  the offsets in the super; prints the region in the layout.
- tools/chk_mxfs.c: validates the region against the slice count and the
  device, registers it in the overlap check, prints its offsets, and
  `check_slife` reports every slice's state (a ZEROING slice is called out:
  a claimant's zero did not reach READY); `--upgrade-protogate` refuses a
  volume without the region, since only mkfs can lay it out.
- tests/d0531_stale_slice_recovery.sh: the variant arm now asserts the
  plant is on the platter before the claim and GONE at the crash (foreign
  headers 0), and both arms assert the first-mount window carries
  `P-SLIFE slot=0 slice=0 before=INIT_REQUIRED after=READY` with no refusal
  and no legacy skip, that the claim's `payload_off` equals the slice
  offset `tools/slice_image.py geom` derives independently from the
  envelope and the XFS superblock, and that its length equals the slice.
  A state machine reporting READY says nothing about where it acted; only
  the platter-side assertions carry the verdict.  Verified on
  9A5DB6C72979614DBF845A6 (s61b,
  tests/evidence/20260919T025452Z_d0531ssr_s61b): the variant arm planted
  34457 old blocks (2872 foreign headers, verify OK) into slot 0's freshly
  formatted slice; the first mount's claim reported `before=INIT_REQUIRED
  after=READY zeroed_bytes=66781184 zero_ms=4334` at payload_off
  27071496192 = the image tool's log_phys; the crash image carried 1 header,
  0 foreign; recovery mounted, 40 of 40 witness files back with content,
  0 refusals, home dinode FREE before and ALLOCATED after — the variant row
  equals the control's.  Zero shutdown, BUG or Oops; both nodes mounted and
  writable afterwards; the offline `chk_mxfs -v` after the lap (both nodes
  unmounted; chk_offline_after_lap.txt in the evidence directory) reports
  every region OK, 32 slices with 30 INIT_REQUIRED and 2 READY and 0
  invalid, and 0 errors.  The measured wall was 759 s and the harness bound is tightened
  from 1400 s to 1000 s.  Removed: D-SLICE-CLAIM-TIME-INIT-UNTRUSTED-ZERO-531
  (FIXED AND VERIFIED).  Open on purpose: the per-record incarnation stamp
  (ruling item (c)), tracked in docs/slice-lifecycle.md.

## 2026-09-19 — 0.87.23 — one inode-chunk carve per allocation: a refusal storm can no longer spend a create's reservation into a shutdown

- xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c: `mxfs_dialloc_carve_gate` — both chunk-carve arms
  of `xfs_dialloc_try_ag` (the empty-AG carve and the swept retry) now pass
  one gate, and one `xfs_dialloc` call may carve ONE chunk.  The create's
  transaction reserves `XFS_IALLOC_SPACE_RES`, space for exactly one chunk;
  the rest of its reservation belongs to the directory entry and parent
  pointer it still has to write, which the allocator cannot see, and
  `xfs_trans_roll` carries only the remainder forward.  Upstream never
  carves twice because after a carve the pick cannot fail; MXFS's
  candidate refusals can make it fail, and the swept retry then carved
  again on every re-sweep with the same transaction.  Proven by
  instrument on the two-node TCP rig (s60a, 0.87.22): one create carved 24
  chunks in 2 s — `P-DIALLOC-GROW-RES` blk_res 189 → 29, 21, 13, 5 with
  ialloc_blks=8 — then `xfs_trans_mod_sb` shut the filesystem down at
  blk_res=5 blk_res_used=8 (`P-TRANS-BLKRES-OVERRUN`), the node withdrew,
  20 of 20 creates failed and the mount stayed unwritable until re-formed.
  The credit is spent when `xfs_ialloc_ag_alloc` succeeds and before the
  roll; a second carve is refused with `P-DIALLOC-CARVE-BOUND` and the AG
  handed back as -EAGAIN, which the sweep already treats as a transient
  refusal.  `rs->swept` is reset at every AG visit so one AG's vote never
  carves in the next; `P-DIALLOC-RESV-SWEPT` now prints pubpend and the
  vote.  Design consult (Astra) ruled the count is the only honest bound
  and that the vote itself must stay: a first cut that cast `swept` only on
  peer contention hung a create whose sole free number was refused for
  good (harness phase 2: 1088 re-sweeps at 5-300 ms, parent ILOCK held,
  test1 power-cycled twice) — that lesson is in `docs/free-publish.md`
  ("One inode-chunk carve per allocation") and ccmemory.
- xfs/xfs_trans.c: `P-TRANS-BLKRES-OVERRUN` names the task, the reservation
  and the consumption at the `xfs_trans_mod_sb` guard before the shutdown,
  so an overrun is attributed by instrument rather than by reading code.
- tests/d0947_nomagic_repick.sh: phase 3 now asserts no allocation carved a
  second chunk (`P-DIALLOC-GROW-RES grows>1` = 0) and no reservation
  overrun (`P-TRANS-BLKRES-OVERRUN` = 0), and reports the second-carve
  refusals.  Verified 2 of 2 laps on 7F7F5FEC4E533781AEFA22E (s60e, s60f,
  tests/evidence/20260919T012424Z_d0947nomagic_s60e and
  20260919T012509Z_d0947nomagic_s60f): every phase PASS, storm phase 20/20
  creates in 16.2 s and 16.5 s, 136 storm exits per lap, max grows=1, 32
  second carves refused in the first lap and 0 in the second (the first
  lap's chunk still had free inodes), zero shutdown, zero withdraw, both
  nodes mounted and writable after each lap; then the capture gate's own
  healthy lap of the harness (s60g) PASS in 29 s.  The manifest bound is
  tightened from 120 s to 90 s toward that wall.  Removed:
  D-DIALLOC-REPICK-STORM-OVERRUNS-THE-TRANSACTION-BLOCK-RESERVATION-SHUTDOWN
  (FIXED AND VERIFIED).  Left open on purpose, as liveness rather than
  accounting: a create whose every candidate keeps being refused after its
  one carve backs off at a bounded rate with no deadline, and the 64-restart
  budget is never reset within a call.
- tests/d0531_stale_slice_recovery.sh: the variant arm plants the previous
  incarnation's records between the fresh format and the lone mount, from
  the node that just ran mkfs and is not yet registered, instead of
  composing them into the crash image afterwards from a second node — the
  post-crash plant was refused with a reservation conflict (s54z: an
  unregistered initiator cannot write while the dead incarnation's Write
  Exclusive all-registrants reservation stands), and the rig's LUN is the
  QNAP appliance target (data/rigs.json), not a device the host serves, so
  there is no backing store to write around it.  The platter at the crash
  is the same; the first mount now also runs on the stale slice, which is
  what a non-durable mkfs zero leaves.  The first mount's own kernel-log
  window (from a marker) and the crash image's foreign-header count are
  asserted, so the recovery is proven to face the old records.
- tools/slice_image.py: the direct-write path released no memoryview over
  its mmap, so closing the mmap raised BufferError after every block had
  been written and fsynced — the plant landed and the tool reported failure
  (s60h).  Each view is released in a context manager before the close.
  `compose --keep-first N` leaves the first N blocks as the base image has
  them: with block 0 planted too, the fresh incarnation's first mount was
  refused at head discovery (mismatched uuid, error -117, s60i) and never
  wrote a record, so the crash the record is about was unreachable; a zero
  block 0 reads as a completely zeroed log, the mount proceeds, and the old
  records sit beyond the genuine head.
- xfs/xfs_inode.h, xfs/xfs_inode.c, xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c (from session 59,
  first built and deployed in this version): `XFS_ILOCK_MXFS_NOEND`, an
  unlock-only flag meaning no inode-DLM end is owed; `xfs_iunlock` skips
  the holder decrement and BAST path when it is set, `mxfs_ilock_fallible`'s
  give-up path passes it, and the -EHOSTDOWN arm of `mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin`
  now tells a fallible caller it gave up (`mxfs_acqfall_give_up_rc(ino,
  -EIO)`), so a stat aborted by the recovery-blocked cutoff no longer runs
  an end with no matching begin (`P71-UNDERFLOW`).  Not yet verified
  against its record; D-STAT-ABORTED-BY-THE-RECOVERY-BLOCKED-CUTOFF-ENDS-
  ITS-INODE-DLM-HOLD-UNPAIRED stays in the queue with its lap as the next
  step.

## 2026-09-19 — 0.87.22 — the formation test heals a phantom upgrade deny the way the kernel does; a one-lap gate driver; seven release-bar records adjudicated from their evidence

- tests/tauth/formation_test: the worker records its first failure (which
  request, the local held mode, the rc, the call wall) and the master's
  upgrade-deny count, and on -EDEADLK while holding NL does what the
  kernel's ilock layer does for a phantom entry (P109-EDEADLK-NL): the
  unconditional release to the current master, then a fresh acquire.
  Measured 3 x 8 runs (tests/evidence/formation_s59/): with no handling 3 of
  8 runs failed, every failure an EX denied -35 at local mode NL with
  P-CONVBLK-DENY equal to the failure count and zero budget give-ups; with
  unlock-and-retry alone 5 of 8 failed, the deny repeating through all ten
  laps because an unlock of nothing sends nothing; with the healing 8 of 8
  pass, six phantom denies each cleared in one lap.  The record
  D-FORMATION-TEST-LOCK-REQUESTS-FAIL-EDEADLK-...-0968 is removed: not an
  engine defect, a harness asserting one layer below where the designed
  refusal is handled.
- tests/capture_gate_sweep.sh: one healthy lap of the capture gate per
  call (`lap`), bounded by the manifest entry's own healthy timeout, then
  each node's mount and a real write through it (`fleet`), and a bounded
  restore (`ensure`, ssh wait then prep_cluster once) — so a delegated
  runner never waits on anything longer than a manifest bound and a lap
  after a kill-arm or shutdown-producing harness starts on a restored
  fleet.  The session-58 chunk manifests lived in a scratchpad; this
  replaces them.
- tests/capture_gate.manifest: tcp_lockreq_blackhole runs the gate with
  ARMED_S=180 (one acquire budget, the header's minimum) and the header's
  derived 364 s bound; the 604 s bound was for the default 420 s arming,
  which the gate does not need.
- The release-bar adjudications recorded on the ledger, each from the
  record's own evidence: two verification instruments stay on the list
  (chk_mxfs walks no directory entries; the structural audit gate proves no
  exposure); four pace records leave it with their measured completion (the
  35-80 s clean-unmount handoff, the 10 s mount BAST wait, the in-barrier
  ledger purge, the unit-attention detection latency); the unpaired stat
  end is inert by code reading (count clamped, every release arm gated on
  BAST or CACHED, observed at state NONE) and its cause is the -EHOSTDOWN
  arm never telling a fallible caller it gave up, fix recorded; the remount
  refusal is renamed for its measured cause — a same-boot successor mount
  fenced by a concurrently mounting peer whose 10 s retire grace expired
  0.9 s before the successor's own 8.6 s settle of its predecessor's record.

record stays open pending the gate laps recorded below) and the gate side of
D-A-TEST-HARNESS-CAN-REPORT-A-VERDICT-ABOUT-MXFS.  No kernel code changed.

The device inventory was 130 sites in 118 scripts choosing a block device by
a path that exists on one rig only; counting the TCP rig's own `/dev/sdX`
spelling (a path member of the multipath map on the other rig) made it 203
in 159.  It is now 0 unadjudicated, 40 adjudicated by reading.  The design
consult's ruling shaped the fix: discovery finds a candidate, an independent
declaration says which LUN is intended, and a marker filled from whatever
prep happened to select would certify the wrong disk after formatting it.

- data/rigs.json declares each rig's shared LUN by its SCSI identifier under
  the tag tools/mxfs_rig_tag.sh prints (this rig: the QNAP LUN's NAA WWID);

  resolved path, major:minor, WWID (sysfs, or the multipath map's dm uuid,

## 2026-09-18 — 0.87.19 — every remote substitution that fed a verdict crosses the boundary; the polling wait and the workload read have a shape; a rejection gate per harness

Work on D-A-TEST-HARNESS-CAN-REPORT-A-VERDICT-ABOUT-MXFS (the record stays
open pending the laps recorded below).  No kernel code changed.

The 335 verdicts fed by an unvalidated remote substitution (the class the
second consult added, 61 files) are now 0, and so are the count-fed
assertions.  Most moved mechanically; the shapes that needed a decision:

- A POLLING wait that ended in a verdict (`t=$(waitfor node PAT 60)`, 24
  sites in four harnesses) could not tell a line the kernel never logged
  from an ssh that never ran — every failed poll read as a count of zero
  and the harness printed a FAIL about MXFS.  `wait_for_into` (tests/lib/
  rig.sh) polls the same way, then makes the FINAL window cross the boundary
  (status, WINDOW_END, the mark present) before it may say `timeout`.
- A command that IS the workload — the read of the file under test, its
  digest, an xattr, a PR OUT whose refusal is the finding — has no shape to
  impose, because the content is the result.  It now reports its own status
  on a line of its own (`printf '\nREAD_RC=%s\n' $?`; printf, because a
  `head -c 4` read has no final newline and `echo` would glue the record to
  the bytes) and that line is the shape; the ssh's status is what ABORTs,
  and the harness's own parse runs over the capture minus the record.  An
  empty digest is then the node failing to read, never an ssh that did not
  run.
- A PERSISTENT RESERVE IN is the exception with a shape: an answered one
  carries `PR generation=`, an error message does not (the sess41 probe
  that parsed sg_persist's error text into "keys=0").  pr_preempt_sark0 and
  pr_session_drop require it; pr_preempt also resolves the LUN from W's
  live mount instead of the QNAP by-path it hardcoded.
- `window_into` (the marked or whole ring across the boundary, for the
  harnesses that extract a field from it rather than count), `wait_for_into`
  and the mid-line reassignment (`stmt; r=$(cat file)` untaints r) in the
  lint.
- scripts/harness_cnt_rewrite.py: `--shape remote --only-lint` (a bare
  `$(rs …)`, `$(rsx …)` or `$(timeout N $SSH …)` feeding a verdict, the
  result shape inferred from the command — its echoed tag, `stat -c %i`,
  srcversion, a knob read, `grep -c` with `|| [ $? = 1 ]` appended for its
  legitimate-zero status, md5sum, `date +%s`, a `sed -n 's/^tag=//p'` pipe
  — into value_now_into, measure + a local pipe, window_into + a local
  extract, or the READ_RC form; polling loops are left alone because the
  lint is what names the sites); `--shape waitfor`; `--shape header` (the
  local filt()/rs() pair replaced by the library source); `--shape value`
  takes N helper arguments.  118 + 12 + 25 + 34 + 24 substitutions moved by
  the tool, 36 sites by hand (pr_preempt's sg_persist wrappers, d0947's
  three-phase producers and counts, d0531/lone_mount's boot and unmount

- docs/harness-capture-contract.md: the parent-assigned primitives, the
  workload form, the injection, the gate and the rewriter.
- tests/rig_lib_contract.sh: case 20 adjudicated (its counts are of the
  library's own fault record); s57a PASS 31/31 in 17 s on test1.

- tests/dlm_wait_signal.sh: its healthy lap FAILed "reader did not spin
  (max stime < 100 ticks)" from `max_stime_ticks=none` — no stime sample
  existed, and the harness read the absence as a spin.  The reader was gone

## 2026-09-18 — 0.87.18 — the capture boundary reaches every counted verdict; parent-assigned counts and values; a library-level fault lap

Work on D-A-TEST-HARNESS-CAN-REPORT-A-VERDICT-ABOUT-MXFS (the record stays
open).  No kernel code changed.

The second design consult (2026-09-18) widened the class: a verdict fed by a
VALUE straight from a remote substitution (`ck "size" "$(rs 20 B "stat -c %s
f")" 0`, `x=$(rs …); ck … "$x"`, `$(cnt PAT)` where cnt runs ssh) is the same
defect as a count over an empty capture.  A fabricated FAIL is still a
verdict taken from no measurement, and a producer can print the expected
scalar and then fail, so "fails closed" can PASS.  Measured by the lint once
it looked: 457 such verdicts in 62 harnesses, against the 72 count-fed
assertions the previous control had reached.

- tests/lib/rig.sh: `count_file_into` (a count over a validated capture,
  assigned in the parent with printf -v, grep's own failure an ABORT);
  `window_count_into var node t mark pattern tag` (the marked kernel ring
  into its own sequence-numbered file, the run-to-end sentinel AND the mark
  required — a window without its mark reads every count as zero — then
  counted locally); `value_now_into` (exactly one result line or ABORT, a
  value printed before a failing exit caught by the status record);
  `prep_require` (a node-preparation capture must carry NODE_PREP_OK; a
  NODE_PREP_FAIL or no record is an ABORT even when a later command in the
  same list succeeded); `MXFS_FAULT_RSX_NTH=<n>` in `rsx` (the n-th
  measurement of any adopted harness is issued to a host that does not
  resolve, the sequence kept in a file so subshells count too, the STAGE
  FAULT line on stderr the proof the injection was reached); `rs` closes
  stdin like `rsx`.

  `value_now_into` and guard functions that pass a positional file to them;
  learns bounded loop variables (`for n in $A $B` guards `dmesg_$n` when
  both named captures are guarded); and reports a second class, verdicts
  fed by a remote substitution or by a variable last assigned from one,
  per file's own remote helpers (any function that runs $SSH or calls one).
- scripts/harness_cnt_rewrite.py: moves `cnt`-style per-assertion remote
