## 2026-09-12 — 0.85.0 — a dead node's open extent-free intents are completed by the survivor under retained custody on the TCP transport, instead of refusing the slice and quarantining its allocation groups

D-FOREIGN-SLICE-INTENTS-ABANDONED, measured on 0.84.24 (sess610,
tests/d_intents_2tcp_open_efi.sh s610h): a victim virsh-destroyed inside an
EFD hold left one open EFI in its slice; the survivor's replay refused the
slice (P226-FR-INTENTS-UNDISCHARGED, P241-RECOV-TERMINAL reason=8), the
victim's allocation group answered EIO to the survivor's own mkdir, the two
extents the EFI named stayed allocated with no owner, and the returned
victim's mount was refused, so an ordinary rm interrupted by a crash left a
two-node cluster at one node until an operator repaired the volume.

What the survivor does now, on the TCP transport only (the CAW transport
keeps the terminal refusal; it has no custody model):

- The census verdict flips to P226-FR-INTENTS-RECOVERABLE when every open
  intent is an EFI, the AG-scoped list exported, nothing quarantines
  filesystem-wide, the mounted volume has neither rmapbt nor reflink and
  `mxfs.obl_complete_enable=1` (the A/B knob, default on).  The replayer
  parks the list (P-OBL-PARK) or a zero census; the ladder's durable
  IMAGES_REPLAYED CAS writes the list (P226-OBL-WRITE) and carries the OPEN
  record or CENSUS_ZERO in the same CAS.  A ladder entered below that
  milestone with nothing parked is HELD (P234-COMPLETE-NOCENSUS), and
  GRANTS_RELEASED refuses an OPEN record and an undecided census
  (P234-RECOV-OBL-UNDECIDED).
- The OPEN branch of the completion ladder (read back from the platter,
  never from the parked copy) installs a filesystem-layer freeze over the
  record's AGs through the disklock callback, retires the dead node's grants
  at once (`v5_dead_grants_retire`: note-dead, lease unregister, remaster
  refresh, ledger purge, table purge, page handoff — factored from the
  ladder's step 2b and idempotent), and hands the case to the worker
  (P-OBL-OPEN, outcome OBLIGATIONS_OPEN).  Retiring before OBLIGATIONS_DONE
  is safe because the victim's slice is durably home at IMAGES_REPLAYED and
  nobody re-replays past it.  The retirement marker is keyed on the victim
  incarnation epoch AND the publication sequence: the list's seq restarts at
  1 per case, so a marker keyed on seq alone matched the NEXT victim in the
  same slot, skipped the remaster/purge trio, and left the custodian's AG
  acquire queued behind a dead holder for its whole 61 s budget four times
  (s612c).
- The freeze (`m_mxfs_oblf_*`, `mxfs_oblf_note`) is one entry per victim slot
  keyed (epoch, seq); its union is checked at the top of `__mxfs_ag_dlm_lock`
  after the quarantine check and before every fast path.  A non-blocking
  caller gets -EAGAIN (P-OBLF-AG-EAGAIN, the allocator moves to another AG);
  a blocking caller waits on the lift, bounded by the 120 s dead-holder
  budget (P-OBLF-AG-WAIT / P-OBLF-AG-TIMEOUT, never a bypass).  The custodian
  task and a transaction already retaining the AG's grant are exempt.  Every
  node installs it from the platter: the ladder's own callback, the disklock
  monitor per readable sector per pass (an invalid or undecided record at
  IMAGES_REPLAYED freezes the whole filesystem for that slot,
  P-OBLF-INSTALL-INVALID), and a synchronous 64-sector scan at mount
  registration so a joiner's freeze exists before its first allocation.
  Lifted per slot (P-OBLF-LIFT) at or past OBLIGATIONS_DONE, terminal, or
  gone.
- The engine (`xfs/xfs_mxfs_recov_obl.c`, the worker's OBLIGATIONS_OPEN arm):
  re-read record and list from the platter, re-check the list against the
  mounted geometry, feature-gate, wait for the AG to be quiet, then per
  extent ONE tr_itruncate transaction: blocking AG lock, fix_freelist,
  `xfs_alloc_has_records`: EMPTY frees the extent (ANY_OWNER, busy extent),
  FULL skips, SPARSE is terminal reason 9 OBLIGATION_UNRECONCILABLE over the
  record's mask.  FULL and SPARSE commit the transaction (a dirty cancel
  after an AGFL refill is a shutdown).  Then log force, home flush, the
  two-phase proof (P-OBL-DONE-WRITE), OBLIGATIONS_DONE (stage 5 + F_DONE,
  P234-RECOV-OBLIGATIONS-DONE), the lift, P-OBL-COMPLETE, and the ordinary
  publication.  A test hold `mxfs.dbg_obl_engine_hold_ms` parks the engine
  after its first extent commits.
- Takeover: the worker defers a case while any other dead slot is
  non-terminal and below IMAGES_REPLAYED (P-OBL-DEFER: a prior custodian's
  committed frees must be home before any bnobt query); the mount barrier
  never completes a case inside mount but hands OPEN slots to the post-mount
  worker (P-OBL-BARRIER-OPEN).
- `tools/chk_mxfs --show-quarantine` decodes the OPEN/DONE record, the list
  and the proof, names reason 9; `--free-query AGNO:AGBNO:LEN` answers
  FREE / ALLOCATED / PARTIAL for an extent from the platter.
- `docs/dlm-protocol.md` "As built on the TCP transport (0.85.0)" records the
  design and why a freeze at the AG-lock choke point replaces the CAW
  transfer/receipt machinery here.

Measured on this build (F2428B3F7E00AE4CDB2AC38, tests/evidence/
20260913T032751Z_intents2tcp_s613a and 20260913T033016Z_intents2tcp_s613b,
MODE=complete with CHURN=1 and CHURN=0): the replay succeeded with the OPEN
case, the engine freed 2 of 2 census extents (EMPTY->freed, none FULL, none
SPARSE), the proof committed, OBLIGATIONS_DONE landed, the slot was published
only after it, zero P241-RECOV-TERMINAL, zero P240-QUAR, zero freeze
timeouts, the survivor's create inside the former mask and at the root both
succeeded, both extents read FREE on the platter, the churn arm ran 210
create/remove rounds inside the frozen AG with zero errors, and the victim
remounted and created in its former directory; walls 136 s and 139 s,
fails=0 on 34 assertions each.  The custodian-kill arm of the same harness
failed on this build (neither node could remount): that is 0.85.1.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.24 — a freed platter image read with no fresh grant is not a verdict on a cached directory, so a peer's mkdir under a directory the other node just recreated no longer answers ESTALE

Measured on the 2026-09-12 two-node TCP board (fence_during_write row,
run_id 20260912T221211Z, both nodes' kernel logs, 22:19:53-55, ino 10594)
and then made deterministic: node B removes a directory and recreates it on
the same inode number, its new dinode is only logged, and the parent's
release drain makes the dirent visible while the platter still holds the
post-free image (mode 0, generation old+1).  Node A still holds a referenced
in-core inode of the previous incarnation.  Its lookup cache-hits that
shell; the directory consumer refresh then reloads it BEFORE taking any
grant, reads the freed image, and the reload's corpse arm — clean shell,
free image, different generation — poisoned the shell as a dead
incarnation.  The poison is sticky, so the acquire that followed a
millisecond later, which BASTed B, drained the true dinode and read it,
could no longer adopt the live incarnation, and every create under the
directory was refused -ESTALE at entry (`P34H-INCARN-POISON src=reload
disk_mode=0`, then `P240-QUAR-NSOP-REFUSE op=create rc=-116`).  The same
window is met by xfs_lookup's stale-flagged arm when the eviction ring's
freed event has already arrived: its grant-less raw read of the dinode saw
the free image, four evictions cache-hit the same referenced shell, and the
old shell was returned as an existing directory.

Two sites, one rule: a freed image read with no fresh grant may not condemn
a shell, because a creator's undrained new incarnation of the number reads
exactly like a genuinely freed slot.

- `mxfs_dlm_reload_inode` (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c) now takes the verdict only
  under a fresh wire grant.  The one reload taken inside the acquire slow
  path, after the previous holder's drain, calls
  `mxfs_dlm_reload_inode_under(..., under_grant=true)` and may still
  poison; every other caller (the consumer refresh before its acquire, the
  iget paths, readdir, the file paths) goes through the grant-less
  signature, and a free different-generation image there logs
  `P346-INCARN-DEFER`, releases the buffer and leaves the shell stale for
  the acquire's own reload to judge.  The dirty-provenance keep is
  unchanged and still precedes it.
- xfs_lookup's stale-flagged arm (xfs/xfs_inode.c), on a raw read of mode 0
  for a name a published parent just resolved, takes one coordinated PR
  acquire on the number (`mxfs_dlm_force_peer_flush`: the request BASTs the
  creator's published EX, whose release drain destages the new dinode, and
  the acquire's slow-path reload adopts the live incarnation in place) and
  re-reads before deciding (`P346-REUSE-COORD`, `P346-REUSE-COORD-READ`).
  A genuinely free number gets an uncontended acquire, still reads free,
  and the arm behaves as before.

Reproducer and verification, `tests/d0346_reuse_dir_mkdir.sh`: the creator
recreates the directory with the just-freed number (a sync between the
remove and the recreate flushes inodegc, otherwise the next number is
taken), and the window is held open rather than raced for.  Three things
the harness had to learn on the way, each measured as ten vacuous rounds:
xfsaild destages the new dinode within milliseconds on a quiet rig (s609d);
the iflush-pause knob is keyed on the inode xfsaild pushes, and a parent in
the same inode cluster carried the child's image as a passenger (s610a), so
the parent is padded into another cluster; and a pause that catches xfsaild
with the parent's own write still on its delayed-write list holds that
write too, so the parent's release drain waited out the pause and the
dirent and the child's dinode landed together (s610b) — the child is pinned
off xfsaild for one kick so the parent lands, then unpinned and its write
paused.  A round counts only when the number was reused, the pause fired,
and the reader's log shows it read the free image.
- Control, 0.84.23 srcversion F1BFDAC2EABAB82C8DF3A29 (s610d,
  tests/evidence/20260913T011221Z_d0346reuse_s610d): 10 of 10 counted
  rounds FAIL — `P34H-INCARN-POISON src=reload disk_mode=0` and
  `P240-QUAR-NSOP-REFUSE op=create rc=-116` for the number on every round.
  The shell retired on the poison-retire loop's first try in this shape,
  so the kernel's retry returned 0 to the user after a 3-4 s stall; on the
  board the previous row's cached children kept the shell unretirable
  (`P34H-POISON-UNRETIRED tries=5`) and the ESTALE reached mkdir.
- Fix, 0.84.24 srcversion 5891B23484D9CA98568B380 (s610e,
  tests/evidence/20260913T011420Z_d0346reuse_s610e): 10 of 10 counted
  rounds OK, zero poison, zero refusal, every create listed by the creator;
  the stale-flagged arm's coordination fired on 2 rounds
  (`P346-REUSE-COORD-READ` re-read mode 040755 with the live generation)
  and the reload's deferral on the other 8, resolved by the acquire's
  reload under grant.  No shutdown, no corruption line, no BUG on either
  node.
- Regression: the 2-node TCP board on this build, run_id 20260913T011856Z
  (tests/evidence/board_2tcp_s610f.log), 26 of 28 rows PASS, including
  fence_during_write (the row that measured the defect),
  dir_reuse_coherency, cache_coherency, dirent_publish_integrity,
  dirent_type_integrity and kernel_health.  The two FAIL rows are one
  event: chk_clean unmounts both nodes, audits (verdict CLEAN, 0 errors),
  and remounts both in the same second; test2's mount was refused because
  test1's persistent-reservation REGISTER landed inside test2's own-key
  proof bracket (`P-PR-BRACKET-INCOHERENT`, `P305-RETIRE-OWN-UNPROVEN
  rc=-71`, `TCP mount REFUSED (-16)`), and tcp_dlm_scaling then found test2
  unmounted.  A single retry mounted test2 in 2.9 s.  That is a mount-time
  fencing defect, nowhere near this change, and it is in the queue as
  D-0965 with the evidence.

With that measurement the record for a peer's mkdir under a recreated
directory answering ESTALE (D-0346) is removed from the queue: FIXED AND
VERIFIED on 2 nodes / TCP.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.23 — the platter judge of a descriptor's holder never reads an unrecognised sector as absence, and its REVOKED verdict is reachable by a native two-node judge

The platter judge (`v5_holder_slot_state`, `dlm/v5_mount.c`) answers
REVOKED for a standing recovery descriptor's holder when the membership
view cannot: the holder's own heartbeat slot is all-zero (published behind a
certified fence), no record in the table carries the tuple, or the record
under the tuple is EMPTY or RETIRE_PENDING.  Two of its readings were
weaker than its own header claimed.  The "all-zero" test compared four
header fields; it now compares the whole 512-byte sector, since a purge and
mkfs write zeros end to end and a sector zero in its header but not its
body is not a published slot.  The table scan skipped any sector without
the disklock magic as "not the holder", so a torn or corrupted record —
possibly the holder's — contributed to "no heartbeat record carries the
holder's tuple", which is REVOKED: absence manufactured from bytes the
judge could not read.  A sector that is neither all-zero nor a record this
build recognises (the disklock magic and a feature block that is the
pre-gate zero tail or carries its own magic) now leaves the verdict UNKNOWN
and names the slot in `P238-FENCE-HOLDER-SLOT`, whether it sits at the
descriptor's owner slot or anywhere in the scan.  Absence proves revocation
only when every record it rests on was read and understood.

Test-only knob `dbg_fence_takeover_decline` (0644, a count): while above
zero, a mount that has proved a FENCING or SNAPSHOTTING attempt's holder
revoked declines to take the attempt over (`P238-FENCE-TAKEOVER-DECLINED`,
one decrement per decline) and everything else runs as shipped.  It exists
because the state the platter judge was written for — a dead holder's
recovery published while an attempt it held still stands — is never
produced by a single two-node mount episode: that episode certifies the
holder's fence, takes over every attempt it held in the same replay round,
and publishes the holder 20 s later (s581a), and node ids are drawn fresh
per mount, so a later mount has no membership route at all.  With the knob
armed, the dead prover's recovery is fenced, replayed and published by the
real writers while its attempt stands; the declined slice holds the mount
barrier and the mount aborts at its bound; the platter is then the s562
state, written by nothing but real fences, replays and purges, and a second
mount with the knob at zero is a native judge of it.
`tests/d0932_platter_fallback.sh` stages and judges that way and asserts the
fail-closed side too (UNKNOWN while the holder's record stood).  Design:
`docs/whole-cluster-restart.md` §7.  The knob's line says "TEST ONLY", not
"DEBUG": the first build's wording carried the substring "BUG:" and every
splat sweep that greps for it counted the 71 declines as 71 splats
(s608b).

Measured on 2 nodes / TCP, srcversion F1BFDAC2EABAB82C8DF3A29, s608c
(tests/evidence/20260912T220017Z_d0932pf_s608c, console
tests/evidence/d0932pf_s608c.console, PASS fails=0, wall 613 s; s608b on
175B4482 measured the same MXFS behaviour with the two harness rows above
scoring falsely):
- Setup: test1 laid a durable FENCING intent for test2's dead incarnation
  and parked (`P236-FENCE-INTENT-HOLD`); destroyed there.  Platter before
  staging: test1's record ACTIVE in slot 0, test2's slot 1 RECOVERY_GUARD
  carrying `stage=FENCING prover=<test1's tuple>`.
- Staging mount (test2's host, knob 1000): 55 `verdict=UNKNOWN` while the
  prover's record stood; the prover's fence certified and `P-DEAD-INC`
  noted it; 71 `P238-FENCE-TAKEOVER-DECLINED`, zero takeovers; the prover's
  slice replayed and published (`P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE slot=0`,
  `P-COMPLETE-TIMING disklock_purge_ms=724`); the declined slice held the
  barrier and the mount aborted at 122 s (rc=32, wall 152 s); zero
  shutdowns or splats.  Platter after: slot 0 gone (all-zero), slot 1
  still carrying the FENCING attempt naming the published prover.
- Judge mount (same host, knob 0, fresh node id, empty dead set): one
  `P238-FENCE-HOLDER-SLOT ... found_slot=-1 verdict=REVOKED — no heartbeat
  record carries the holder's tuple` (the judge had claimed slot 0 for
  itself first, so the descriptor's owner slot read as another tenant and
  the whole-table scan answered), no `P-DEAD-INC` for the prover before it,
  `P238-FENCE-TAKEOVER`, a NEW intent under the victim key frozen from the
  victim's own record, `P236-FENCE-CERTIFIED kind=BOOT_SUCCESSION_ABSENT
  term=2`, `P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE slot=1`, MOUNTED in 21.8 s, zero NOKEY
  or REFUSED, zero shutdowns or splats, no descriptor left on the platter.
- test1's host returned and joined in 2.7 s; both nodes list the same root.
- Regression: the 2-node TCP board on this build, run_id 20260912T223015Z
  (tests/evidence/board_2tcp_s608h.log), 28 of 28 rows PASS, including
  fence_during_write, dirent_durability, chk_clean and kernel_health.

With that measurement the record for a dead prover's fencing attempts
being untakeable (a fencing attempt or unsealed snapshot whose holder died
could be taken over only when the holder's exact incarnation was judged
REVOKED, and the ordinary two-node crash path never noted an incarnation
dead, so the victims' slices stayed frozen and the whole cluster could not
mount) is FIXED AND VERIFIED and removed from the queue: the ordinary route
has noted a certified-fenced incarnation dead since 0.75.74 (measured s581a,
8 of 8), the crash-departed-owner shape has mounted end to end since 0.82.6,
and the platter route a fresh judge with no membership answer depends on is
now reached and answers correctly (s608c above).

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.22 — the fallible acquire class is measured complete at every userspace-reachable boundary; the control harness clears the holder's pause knob before its verdict

No kernel source changed: the module is the 0.84.21 build (srcversion
EC736FCEBFD8078383B2792), and every measurement below was taken on it.

Measurement (`tests/live_holder_wait.sh`): the holder's release-pause knob
(`dbg_rel_pause_ms` / `dbg_rel_pause_ino`) is now cleared on H the moment
W's operation returns, before the verdict's cold pass on H.  Left armed, H's
own re-release of the target — a cold stat after drop_caches re-caches a
grant and the next eviction releases it — paused for another PAUSE_MS inside
the verdict's ssh, which timed out with an empty capture and scored a landed
operation FAIL (s606k-n, s607e/g/i/j: walls 311-320 s and a
P-D512-RELPAUSE-END on H 240 s after the lap had ended).  The fault-control
row that counted the harness's own `<op>_rc=0` marker as a signalled child
now matches only `<op>_rc=-<signal>`.

Design (`docs/dlm-protocol.md`): the fallible-class section carries the
page-fault boundary and the fact that every inode is created with an empty
attr fork, so the add-fork reservation is reached only after the last
attribute is removed.  Budget rows (`tests/criteria/TIMEOUT_BUDGETS.md`)
record the walls below.

Measured on 2 nodes / TCP, 0.84.21, the last laps of the D-0958 class:
- s607k `WORKLOAD=held_fd_setxattr_nofork EXPECT=bounded`
  (tests/evidence/20260912T205005Z_lockreqbh_s607k, fails=0, 396 s): the
  first setxattr on an inode whose attr fork had been removed parked in
  `xfs_trans_alloc_inode`'s ILOCK_EXCL under the discarded request
  (`P958-XATTRSET-PATH has_af=0 forkoff=0`), was refused between +162 s and
  +231 s with `P958-XATTRSET-REFUSED stage=addfork` and EIO to the driver,
  180 requests dropped, the master serving in 3 ms, cancel acked ABSENT, the
  attribute absent on both nodes cold, mode and size unchanged, no shutdown,
  no dirty cancel.
- Controls behind a live holder with its release paused 240 s
  (`PAUSE_MS=240000 MASTER=remote`, all fails=0, zero refusals, zero
  DEGRADED, every wait receipted and landed after H's pause end on H's own
  clock): s607l getxattr 272 s (value v958 on both nodes cold), s607m
  setxattr 269 s (v958 cold on H), s607n mmap_read 270 s (no SIGBUS, bytes
  unchanged and equal), s607o mmap_write 273 s (H's first four bytes cold
  are W's store, digests equal), s607p setxattr_nofork 270 s (fork re-added
  behind the holder, v958 cold on H).
- Full 2/tcp board on 0.84.21 with a fresh prep
  (tests/evidence/board_2tcp_s608a.log, 13 min wall): 28 of 28 PASS,

D-UNRECEIPTED-ACQUIRE-STILL-WAITS-WITHOUT-BOUND-FOR-EVERY-CALLER-THAT-CANNOT-BE-FAILED-0958
is removed from the queue, FIXED AND VERIFIED on 2 nodes / TCP.  The cause:
an inode-lock acquire whose request the live master never receipts
restarted its wait for ever for every caller that could not be failed.  The
fix, ruled by the sess588 design consult and landed site by site from 0.84.0
to 0.84.21: a per-acquisition id with LOCK_CANCEL and master tombstones,
periodic receipts, an operator-visible DEGRADED report, and a fallible
acquire boundary at every userspace-reachable site where nothing is dirty
and no transaction is joined — open, getattr, read, readdir, lookup, the
write path's first ride and timestamp update, the direct-write retries,
create/mkdir/unlink/link/rename/symlink, chmod/chown/utimes, fallocate, the
extended-attribute read, the extended-attribute change (both reservations)
and the page fault.  Each boundary was measured refused inside the armed
window with nothing changed on either node and the cancel acked ABSENT
(`tests/tcp_lockreq_blackhole.sh`, s578e through s607k), and measured
landing behind a live holder paused 240 s with zero refusals and zero
DEGRADED (`tests/live_holder_wait.sh`, s578f through s607p).  A socket-level
fault shorter than the 40 s grace is measured self-healing (s594c).  The
residual non-fallible class (truncate's size transaction, fsync's log-force
ILOCK, writeback, inactivation, AIL, quota) holds state no error return can
put back; by the ruling it waits with exclusion preserved and reports
DEGRADED (s601g measured), and its only producer is a defect in the master's
own lock service.

D-ACQUIRE-TIMEOUT-BEHIND-LIVE-HOLDER-FAILSTOPS-REQUESTER-0912, whose open
TCP remainder that record was, is narrowed to the CAW transport: the
self-shutdown it names has been absent on TCP since 0.75.28 and is
re-measured on every control lap above, so nothing about it on TCP is
unmeasured.  Its CAW lap (a pause longer than CAW's 480 s cap on a 2/caw
prep) has never been run and stays owed in the queue; it is not a gate for
the 2-node TCP release.

Astra was unreachable (HTTP 429, no credits) in this session as in 594 to
607; every step above followed the standing ruling.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.21 — the page fault is a fallible acquire boundary answering SIGBUS, the last userspace-reachable site of D-0958's class; the xattr change's first reservation is instrumented

The page fault (`pal/linux/xfs_file.c`, `xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c`,
`xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.h`).  A read fault takes a counted PR hold directly
(`mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin`, not `xfs_ilock`) before `filemap_fault`; a write
fault first updates the timestamps (`file_update_time` →
`xfs_vn_update_time`, ILOCK_EXCL in a reserved clean transaction) and then
takes a counted EX hold before `iomap_page_mkwrite`.  Each is taken with no
folio locked, nothing dirty and no transaction joined, so a refusal leaves
nothing to undo beyond the hold: `mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin_fallible` registers
the inode around the begin and, on a give-up, calls the hook's end for a
begin that installed nothing (the pairing every other fallible site already
relies on through `xfs_iunlock`); `mxfs_fault_update_time_fallible` registers
the inode around the timestamp update, which cancels its clean reservation
on a refusal.  The fault answers VM_FAULT_SIGBUS and prints
`P958-FAULT-REFUSED ino= stage=read-hold|timestamp|write-hold`.  A stalled
authority transition (-EAGAIN) is not a lost request: a fault has no retry,
so it waits it out as an unregistered caller does.  The nested `xfs_ilock`
inside the iomap path rides the counted hold and sends no request.

Instrument: `xfs_attr_set` prints `P958-XATTRSET-PATH` (first 64, then every
256th) with the attr-fork state it saw, because the s606i lap's fresh file on
a reused inode number reached the change with a fork already present and
was refused at `stage=set` rather than `stage=addfork`; the harness now
accepts either reservation and prints the line.

Measurement: `tests/held_fd_op.py` gains `mmap_read` and `mmap_write` (the
access runs in a forked child so SIGBUS is reported by the parent as
`<op>_rc=-7 SIGBUS`, and the child's pid is published for stack sampling);
`tests/tcp_lockreq_blackhole.sh` gains `WORKLOAD=held_fd_mmap_read` and
`held_fd_mmap_write` (the write arm re-caches W's PR and page cache first, so
the read half is served locally when the stale flag allows) and
`tests/live_holder_wait.sh` the matching `RW=` controls.  The control
harness reads the attribute in the same cold pass as its stat and digest: a
second drop_caches for it (s606k–n) evicted H's freshly cached grant while
the lap's release-pause knob was still armed and parked H's own release for
the pause length, so the capture timed out empty.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.20 — the extended-attribute change is a fallible acquire boundary, the last transactional site of the userspace-reachable class D-0958 named (D-0912's open remainder)

The extended-attribute change (setxattr, removexattr, the security init of
a new inode): `xfs_attr_set` reserves through
`xfs_trans_alloc_inode`, and for an inode with no attr fork yet first runs
`xfs_attr_add_fork`'s reservation the same way; that allocator's ILOCK_EXCL
is the change's first request, taken on a clean unjoined reservation, and
the allocator already asks the registry right after its lock (0.84.15).
Both calls now go through `mxfs_attr_trans_alloc_fallible`
(`xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c`, `xfs/libxfs/xfs_attr.c`), which registers the inode
around the allocator only; a refusal cancels the reservation inside it and
prints `P958-XATTRSET-REFUSED ino= stage=addfork|set|remove`.  The
transaction body after a granted acquire holds ILOCK_EXCL throughout and
takes no further acquire of the inode, so nothing after the boundary can be
refused.

Two items the D-0958 plan listed turn out not to exist in the module, found
while wiring them: FS_IOC_FSSETXATTR / FS_IOC_SETFLAGS are not a site
because `pal/linux/xfs_ioctl.c` is not in Kbuild and `xfs_fileattr_get`/
`_set` are stubs answering -EOPNOTSUPP (`xfs/xfs_stubs.c`); and there is no
ACL read on a permission check because `xfs_acl.o` is excluded.  The 0.84.19
entry's mention of an ACL caller was written from the tree, not the build,
and is wrong; the design doc says which callers exist.

Measurement: `tests/held_fd_op.py` gains `setxattr` (nothing set beforehand,
so the fault meets the add-fork reservation) and `removexattr` (user.d958 set
beforehand, so it meets `xfs_attr_set`'s own); `tests/tcp_lockreq_blackhole.sh`
gains `WORKLOAD=held_fd_setxattr` and `held_fd_removexattr`, and
`tests/live_holder_wait.sh` the matching `RW=` controls.  The 0.84.19
getxattr lap (s606b) had refused correctly but scored two rows FAIL on its
own capture — getfattr printed "Removing leading '/'" on stderr ahead of the
value — so both harnesses now pass `--absolute-names`, and the 0.84.19 laps
are re-measured on this build.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.19 — the extended-attribute read is a fallible acquire boundary, so a getxattr, listxattr, ACL or capability read whose lock request the live master never answers fails with EIO instead of waiting without bound (D-0958, the open remainder of D-0912)

The next site of D-0958's non-fallible class, taken in the order the ledger
set out.  `xfs_attr_get` and `xfs_attr_list` took the attr-fork lock through
`xfs_ilock_attr_map_shared`, a void acquire, so on the TCP transport a request
the live master silently discarded parked the reader for ever (kept and
reported DEGRADED).  The 0.84.15 truncate lap (s601g) showed this is the FIRST
acquire an ftruncate through a held fd sends — `do_truncate` asks
`cap_inode_need_killpriv`, which reads `security.capability` through
`xfs_xattr_get` — ahead of the size transaction; the same read sits inside
exec, `file_remove_privs` on the write path, and every setattr, and the ACL
read sits inside every permission check.

The change (`xfs/xfs_inode.c`, `xfs/xfs_inode.h`, `xfs/libxfs/xfs_attr.c`,
`xfs/xfs_attr_list.c`, `xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c`, `xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.h`): the
attr-fork lock mode is computed once (`xfs_ilock_attr_map_mode`) and shared
by the plain acquire and a new `xfs_ilock_attr_map_shared_fallible`, which
mirrors the data-fork variant readdir uses — `mxfs_ilock_fallible` for the
first take, and the map recheck's relock as a second, separately asked
fallible acquisition.  On a clustered mount both readers take their lock
through it and, on a refusal, return the errno with nothing held and one
line, `P958-XATTR-REFUSED ino= op=get|list rc=`.  Every caller of the two
readers is a boundary — nothing dirty, no transaction — and each returns the
error: getxattr/listxattr to userspace; the capability
read inside truncate, write and setattr reads as "nothing to strip" and the
operation goes on to its own acquire, exactly as upstream treats any error
from that read.  (This entry first also named an ACL read inside permission
checks; the 0.84.20 entry corrects that — ACLs are not compiled into the
module.)  A mount without the cluster overlay takes the unchanged void
acquire.

Measurement: `tests/held_fd_op.py` gains `getxattr` and `listxattr` (the
driver sets `user.d958=v958` on its fd before announcing, so the set's own
EX has landed and been revoked before the read under test, and the value is
known); `tests/tcp_lockreq_blackhole.sh` gains `WORKLOAD=held_fd_getxattr`
and `held_fd_listxattr` (the refusal must be `P958-XATTR-REFUSED` for the
target, the driver gets no `_ok=` line, and the attribute still reads v958
cold on both nodes afterwards); `tests/live_holder_wait.sh` gains
`RW=getxattr` and `RW=listxattr` (the read behind a 240 s paused release
must wait it out and return the value, with no refusal).  Budget rows for
the held-fd attribute workloads, including the 0.84.15 ones that had none,
are in `tests/criteria/TIMEOUT_BUDGETS.md`.  The laps and their evidence
directories are recorded on the D-0958 ledger entry.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.18 — a shortform directory's refresh no longer merges this node's own lagging flush as a peer's image, so a removed entry is not re-added and published as a dangling dirent; D-0963 disposed

D-0963, the one failing row of the 0.84.17 board (cache_coherency
`uv gone node2_file57`: test1 could still stat a name test2 had unlinked and
synced).  The chain, read from both nodes' kernel logs and then reproduced on
demand: a node holding a shortform directory EX refreshes its in-core fork
against the platter before each mutation when the fork is stale-gen (a peer
modified the directory and the re-acquire skipped the rebuild because the
inode was pinned by this node's own not-yet-logged removals — 73 such skips on
test2, loaded_gen frozen at 11 under dir_gen 12).  The refresh runs a 3-way
merge (base / in-core / platter) and re-adds any name that is on the platter,
absent in core and absent from the base, as a peer's fresh add.  xfsaild's
write of the directory inode (all nine `P56-DIRWRITE`s of ino 2246 by
xfsaild/sda, EX held) landed one removal behind the in-core fork; the refresh
read back this node's OWN previous image, still naming the entry just
removed; the base predated every entry this node had created (the directory
had been block format since the creates, so no shortform base was captured);
so the merge re-added the removed name (`P-SFMERGE` 146->166, the name
moving from first to last in the successive write lists) and the last image
the node published held only that name — a dangling dirent naming a freed
inode, listed by both nodes and stat-able on the peer from its cache.

The fix (`xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c`, `xfs/xfs_inode.c`, `xfs/xfs_inode.h`; design in
`docs/shortform-dir-merge.md`): each directory inode keeps a ring of the last
four shortform images this node copied into its inode cluster buffer during
the current EX tenure (recorded in `xfs_iflush`, under ILOCK_SHARED with the
buffer locked, so the bytes are exactly what lands).  When the refresh's
platter read is byte-identical to a ring image it is this node's own
publication and carries no peer change (a peer can modify only while we do
not hold EX), so the in-core fork is authoritative, no merge runs, and the
base advances to that image (`P963-SF-OWN-IMAGE`, counter
`sf_own_image_hits`).  The ring is retired at every release drain, because a
peer's tenure can legitimately recreate an older image of ours byte for byte
by removing what we had added; it is kept inside a tenure, where a base
captured from the pre-tenure platter image must not forget our writes still
in flight.  At an EX release the drain also reads the platter back and
captures it as the merge base (`P963-SF-RELEASE-BASE`, counter
`sf_release_base`): that image is what the peer's tenure builds on, so it is
the true common ancestor for the merge at our next stale-gen re-acquire;
without it, entries added after the last refresh-captured base and deleted by
the peer would read as "ours, changed" and survive.  `sf_own_image=0` is the
control arm on the same build.

Measured, 2 nodes / TCP, build 6BAF3685AFAA6E3EE762338.  The race between
xfsaild's asynchronous write and the coherent read is what a quiet rig loses
(0 of 20 laps of the board criterion with the fix off, s605b,
tests/evidence/20260912T171740Z_d0963cc_control_s605b; 0 of 20 of the
synthetic churn, s604a), so `tests/d0963_sf_lagging_flush.sh` makes the
in-flight window deterministic with test knobs and otherwise takes the real
path: `dbg_ail_pin_ino` keeps xfsaild off the directory inode during the
churn, `sf_fastpath_adopt` (the sess50 lever, now a module parameter) makes
every cached-EX shortform removal take the platter refresh, and
`dbg_iflush_pause_ino`/`_ms` hold xfsaild's cluster write after the copy-in
while the debugfs `ail_push` file starts it on demand.  The creator makes the
directory with three seeds; the deleter lists it (base = the 3-entry image),
creates 64 files, removes them until the directory is shortform again, then
removes V with its own image's write held and W after it lands.
- Control, `sf_own_image=0`, s605d
  (tests/evidence/20260912T174004Z_d0963lag_control_s605d, 3 of 3 laps,
  fails=0 against the control's expectations): each lap `P-SFM-READD
  name=nodeB_file58 base_n=3 ours_n=9 theirs_n=10` and `P-SFMERGE 171->191
  count=10`; after the deleter's sync the name lists on the deleter and cold
  on the creator while stat fails on both — the dangling dirent, published;
  `rm -rf` of the directory then fails with "Directory not empty".
- Fix, `sf_own_image=1`, s605e (20260912T174124Z_d0963lag_fix_s605e) and
  s605f (20260912T174254Z_d0963lag_fix_s605f, 3 of 3 laps, fails=0): each
  lap `P963-SF-OWN-IMAGE disk_count=10 incore_count=9` at W's removal, zero
  `P-SFM-READD`, V and W gone on both nodes, remaining counts equal, the
  own-image counter advancing and images recorded at flush.  (s605e scored
  two false FAILs on the printed-line check — the probe prints its first 32
  hits and then one in 500 — so the harness now reads the counter, reset per
  lap.)
- The board criterion itself, 20 laps with the fix on (s605g,
  tests/evidence/20260912T174350Z_d0963cc_fix_s605g, `tests/d0963_cc_laps.sh`):
  20 of 20 PASS 534/534, zero merges and zero re-adds on either node — the
  race did not occur on the quiet rig in these laps, exactly as with the fix
  off (s605b), so this run is the no-regression check and not the proof; the
  release-time base capture fired 25 times on test2 (`sf_release_base`) and
  190 images were recorded at flush, at no cost to the criterion's wall
  (8-10 s against 9 s before).  The harness reports the own-image arm as
  never fired in these laps rather than counting them as verification.
- Full 2/tcp board on this build with a fresh prep
  (tests/evidence/board_2tcp_s605i.log): 28 of 28 PASS, cache_coherency
  534/534, chk_clean CLEAN.

D-0963 is removed from the queue, FIXED AND VERIFIED, on the measurements
above: the cause proven by ordered log and then reproduced on demand with a
control arm on the same build, the patch at that cause, the fix arm clean on
the same shape with the changed code demonstrably carrying the run, and the
board unchanged.  What the record asked about the checker is measured and
filed on its own evidence: `tools/chk_mxfs -v` run against the volume holding
the control arm's three dangling dirents (tests/evidence/chk_dangling_s605h.log)
reported nothing about any directory — it walks no directory entries at all —
so a dirent naming a free inode reads CLEAN; that is
D-CHK-MXFS-DOES-NOT-WALK-DIRECTORY-ENTRIES-SO-A-DIRENT-NAMING-A-FREE-INODE-PASSES-CLEAN-0964.

Test-only additions, all off by default: `dbg_iflush_pause_ino` /
`dbg_iflush_pause_ms` (`xfs/xfs_inode_item.c`, hold xfsaild's cluster write
after the copy-in; counter `dbg_iflush_pause_n`), the per-mount debugfs
`ail_push` file (start a whole-AIL push on demand; counter `dbg_ail_push_n`),
and `sf_fastpath_adopt` exposed as a module parameter (it was a bare int the
code documented as an A/B lever that no harness could set).  Harnesses:
`tests/d0963_sf_lagging_flush.sh` (the deterministic reproduction, both arms),
`tests/d0963_cc_laps.sh` (the board criterion in a lap loop with the merge
diagnostics armed); `tests/d0963_sf_dirent_resurrect.sh` is kept as the record
of the synthetic shape that could not fire and says why.  Design:
`docs/shortform-dir-merge.md`.  Astra was unreachable (HTTP 429, no credits),
as in sessions 594, 595 and 601; the design was decided from the measurements.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.17 — every create-path recycle can assert on the platter, so the allocator's own-obligation refusal is measured against a control arm that reproduces the D-0946 shutdown on demand; D-0947 disposed

D-0946.  The chain, proven three times on the two-node TCP rig with nothing
killed: xfs_dialloc's candidate validator allowed a number on the strength of
this node's own open FREE obligation (our free committed in core, its image
not yet on the platter), the create's recycle gate (`xfs_iget_recycle`,
`xfs/xfs_icache.c`) then read the platter, found our live predecessor image,
called it cross-node incoherence and returned -EFSCORRUPTED on an already
dirty transaction — a whole-filesystem shutdown.  The fix has been in the
product since 0.75.117-0.75.121: the validator REFUSES such a candidate before
anything is dirtied (`P946-VALIDATE-PUBPEND`), cools it down transiently,
kicks the publication asynchronously and re-picks; `dialloc_pubpend_refuse=0`
keeps the pre-fix arm as the A/B control.  What kept the record open was
verification: the recycle gate's platter read is reached only by a "deferred
deadshell" — a freed shell still carrying a mode or blocks, which ordinary
churn never produces (it took a death/rejoin lap, 3 hits in 16) — so the
control arm had never reproduced the shutdown on demand, and no run had ever
asserted for the fix arm that a handed-out number's platter image is free.

So the verdict the defect ended in is now taken on EVERY create-path recycle
under a test-only knob.  `dbg_recycle_platter_assert=1`
(`xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c`) makes `xfs_iget_recycle` read the recycled number's
home dinode with the coherent plain platter read the allocator itself trusts
(`mxfs_dbg_disk_di_read_coherent`: a private bounce buffer, never the xfs
buffer cache, so nothing cached is staled or re-read on its account) and
fail the recycle with -EFSCORRUPTED when the image is live
(`P946-RECYCLE-ASSERT-DISKLIVE`).  Under the fixed allocator a fire would be
a crossed FREE-PUBLISH invariant and never noise: a FREE obligation is
retired only by the completion of the write carrying the free image
(`docs/free-publish.md`), so a number with no open obligation has a free
home.  Two exact counters, `dbg_recycle_platter_checked` and
`dbg_recycle_platter_live`, prove the check ran (a silent instrument and a
clean system are the same observation), and the allocator's own arm gets
exact counters too — `dialloc_pubpend_refused` / `dialloc_pubpend_allowed`
(`xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c` now counts into them) — because the
`P946-VALIDATE-PUBPEND` / `-ALLOW` lines print the first 32 and then one in
500.  Writing any of the four resets it.  All default 0; the knob is 0 in
production.

Measured, 0.84.17 sv 22D9C2BB319D2C97F39FCE0, 2 nodes / TCP, both nodes
mounted (the validator and the assertion are both disabled for a lone
mount), `tests/d0946_recycle_platter_assert.sh` (new; the tight churn: 400
fallocated files primed, then each round frees one and immediately
re-creates one, twice over, no sync anywhere):
- Fix arm, s603c (tests/evidence/20260912T161438Z_d0946recycle_fix_s603c,
  fails=0): 6 rounds of 800 free+create pairs, every create and unlink
  succeeded, the assertion ran 765-786 times per round and read LIVE zero
  times, the allocator's refusal arm fired 90-240 times per round (so the
  exact code the fix changed was exercised, on numbers it then did NOT hand
  out), zero P-CR63-DEFER-DISKLIVE, zero dirty cancels, zero validator
  quarantines, no shutdown, all 400 files present cold on test2.
- Control arm, s603d (20260912T161544Z_d0946recycle_control_s603d, fails=0):
  the first re-pick of the first round reproduced the whole chain in 2.2 s,
  on inode 132 — the same number as all three original occurrences —
  `P946-VALIDATE-ALLOW via=pubob ino=132 ogen=3224228244` → the assertion
  read `disk_mode=0100644 disk_gen=3224228243` (exactly ogen-1: this node's
  own unpublished free) → `P-CR62 err=-117 verdict=DISK-LIVE` →
  `P-CR3-CANCEL trans_dirty=1` → "Corruption of in-memory data (0x8)
  detected at xfs_trans_cancel ... Shutting down filesystem" → P-WITHDRAW.
  800 of 800 creates then failed on the dead filesystem.  The harness stops
  there and names the re-prep.
- Pace, recorded: a round took 5.9-6.4 s with the assertion on, against
  3.9-4.7 s for the same tight round on 0.75.121 without it — one plain
  platter read per create, test knob only.

The board on this build (tests/evidence/board_2tcp_s603e.log, run_id
20260912T161757Z, fresh prep, build 22D9C2BB319D2C97F39FCE0): 27 of 28
rows PASS, and one FAIL — cache_coherency, 1 of 534 checks on test1,
`uv gone node2_file57`: test1 could still stat a file test2 had unlinked
and synced.  That is a coherency fault in its own right and is filed as
D-PEER-STATS-A-NAME-THE-DELETER-UNLINKED-AND-SYNCED-WHILE-ITS-DIRECTORY-
PUBLICATION-IS-IN-FLIGHT-0963 with the ordered chain from both nodes'
kernel logs: the deleter's shortform directory was published by xfsaild as
nine separate writes, one name fewer each, AFTER its sync returned; the
verifier adopted the platter image mid-sequence with the one remaining name
(`P43-ADOPT-PEER-SHRINK disk_size=26`, `P62-DUALREAD verdict=PLATTER-IS-OLD`),
its own lookups could not reload the directory under their ILOCK_SHARED
(`P173-RELOAD-SELFREAD`, `P212-RDRETRY-SKIP` "serving consistent-stale") and
the name's inode was still live in its cache until `P116-ZOMBIE-ADOPT`.  No
step of that chain is an inode allocation, every create-bearing row passed,
and the same row passed 534/534 on the 0.84.16 board eleven minutes
earlier on the same fleet; 0.84.17 changes nothing on that path.

D-0946 is removed from the queue, FIXED AND VERIFIED, on the measurements
above: the cause proven by ordered log (two gates contradicting each other
about a legal state), the patch at that cause (refuse before dirtying, per
the ruling), the control arm reproducing the shutdown on demand and the
fix arm asserting the platter free on every re-pick with the changed code

board's create-bearing rows.  Not carried by the disposition, so it is not
lost: the ruling's long-term proof-carrying reuse token is design work; the

consequence of the shutdown this removes and has not recurred; the refusal
costs ~13 percent on the tight micro-loop and nothing on the board.

D-0947 is removed from the queue, FIXED AND VERIFIED, on the 0.84.16 board:
- **Every file create on a healthy, mounted, 7%-full two-node filesystem
  fails with EIO, permanently, once the inode allocator's search reaches an

  C91615EEFBD155E1DDE308D by injection at the verdict
  (`tests/d0947_nomagic_repick.sh`, 27/27 twice, s602c/s602d — see 0.84.16

  (tests/evidence/board_2tcp_s603b.log, run_id 20260912T155327Z: fio_perf

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.15 — chmod/chown/utimes and fallocate take their first acquire as a fallible boundary; the residual class is measured under its DEGRADED report

D-0958, the last two userspace-reachable sites whose first cluster acquire
sits on nothing dirty, plus the measurement of what remains.

**The attribute change.**  `xfs_setattr_nonsize` (`pal/linux/xfs_iops.c`)
reaches its first cluster acquire inside `xfs_trans_alloc_ichange`
(`xfs/xfs_trans.c`): `tr_ichange` reserved, `xfs_ilock(ILOCK_EXCL)` — a
cluster EX — and only then the join and the quota reservation.  The caller
now goes through `mxfs_trans_alloc_ichange_fallible` (`xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c`),
which registers the inode around the allocator; both allocators
(`xfs_trans_alloc_ichange`, `xfs_trans_alloc_inode`) ask
`mxfs_acqfall_refused` right after their lock, at the point where the
existing quarantine gate already sits, and on a refusal cancel the clean,
unjoined reservation, drop the lock and return -EIO.  The wrapper names the
operation (`P958-SETATTR-REFUSED op=chmod|chown|utimes`).  Only a registered
task ever takes that branch; every other caller of the two allocators waits
exactly as before.  The dquots a chown allocated before the transaction are
released on the caller's ordinary error path.

**fallocate.**  `__xfs_file_fallocate` (`pal/linux/xfs_file.c`) begins with
`xfs_ilock(IOLOCK_EXCL | MMAPLOCK_EXCL)` and nothing precedes it; that take
is now `mxfs_ilock_fallible`, a refusal returns -EIO holding nothing
(`P958-FALLOCATE-REFUSED`), and `file_modified` inside runs unregistered on
the grant the take established.

**A refusal line that printed garbage.**  `xfs_file_dio_write_aligned`
passed the boolean `true` where the ride's stage name goes, so an aligned
direct write's refusal printed `stage=(efault)`; it now says `stage=first`.
The ride was fallible all along (any non-NULL stage is).

**What 0.84.14 measured**, deployed as 56D888F713409EA0BB18DD6 and never
written down: s596g (`WORKLOAD=held_fd_dio_unaligned EXPECT=bounded`,
tests/evidence/20260912T132629Z_lockreqbh_s596g) was refused at the write's
first shared ride, not at the timestamp — the re-cached PR did not serve
that ride because the cached-PR fast path also requires the inode's stale
flag clear — bounded, EIO, nothing written, correct after the disarm, cancel
acked ABSENT; s596h (`HOLDER=pr RW=dio_unaligned PAUSE_MS=240000`,
tests/evidence/20260912T133343Z_livewait_s596h) landed the write behind the
paused PR release at 242 s with both nodes reading it (the holder paused two
drains 0.5 s apart because its EX-to-PR demote from the re-cache read was
still in the bast worker when the pause was armed; both ended).  The
registration is narrowed in this build to `file_update_time` alone:
`file_remove_privs` runs setattr/xattr transactions with no refusal check
and waits as before.

**Measured on 0.84.15** (sv 5C4B92790DF424A5313E987, 2 nodes / TCP, both
nodes confirmed on that srcversion before every lap):

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.13 — the lookup and the direct-write retries are fallible boundaries; a stale re-send is refused by name at the master

D-0958, three pieces.

**The lookup.**  `xfs_lookup` (`xfs/xfs_inode.c`) acquires the parent twice:
the consumer refresh, and the directory read inside `xfs_dir_lookup`, whose
own `xfs_ilock_data_map_shared` carries the acquire.  Both are now audited
boundaries (nothing dirty, no transaction, the VFS holds only the parent's
i_rwsem).  `xfs_ilock` returns void and takes the local lock whether or not
the grant came, so `xfs_dir_lookup` (`xfs/libxfs/xfs_dir2.c`) asks, right
after its lock and before it reads a block, whether the acquire it rode was
refused (`mxfs_acqfall_refused`, `xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c`): a refused lookup
reads nothing, caches nothing, and the registering caller
(`mxfs_dir_lookup_fallible`) turns the verdict into the errno the path walk
reports (`P958-LOOKUP-REFUSED stage=refresh|dir`).

**The direct-write retries.**  The unaligned exclusive retry of
`xfs_file_dio_write_unaligned` and the COW retry of
`xfs_file_dio_write_atomic` (`pal/linux/xfs_file.c`) were left blocking in
0.84.10 on the assumption that the -EAGAIN / -ENOPROTOOPT they follow might
come after part of the range was submitted.  Read from the reference
(`fs/iomap/direct-io.c`, `xfs_direct_write_iomap_begin`): under
IOMAP_OVERWRITE_ONLY the first mapping must span the whole request with one
written extent or answer -EAGAIN at the first `->iomap_begin`, before any bio
exists, and the bio iterator itself never produces -EAGAIN; an atomic write
is one extent or -ENOPROTOOPT at the same first mapping.  So each retry
follows an attempt that moved no bytes, and its ride is now fallible
(`P958-WRITE-REFUSED stage=unaligned-excl-retry|atomic-cow-retry`), a
refusal being -EIO for a write that landed nothing.

**The stale re-send.**  Caught by chance in s594c: a re-send of a LOCK_REQ
that left before its grant arrived, whose sender then consumed the grant and
released it, reached the master after the release and was queued as a fresh
request — the sender's entry was gone — and, being compatible, granted at
once to a wait that no longer existed; the sender bounced it
(`P958-ACQ-GRANT-BOUNCED`), and between the phantom grant and the bounce the
master believed the sender held a lock it knew nothing about.  Now
(`dlm/dlm.c`): LOCK_RELEASE carries `acq_done`, set when the releaser has no
live acquisition record for that resource and mode (a wait still re-sending
under that name, whose grant was released under it before the claim, keeps
`acq_done=0` and is still served); on a release with `acq_done` the master
tombstones `{sender, owner incarnation, acq_seq}` in a 256-slot consumed
ring, after the stale-generation and incarnation checks so an overtaken
release can never tombstone the name a re-affirm re-stamped onto a live
entry; a later LOCK_REQ carrying a tombstoned name is refused with the same
silence as a cancelled one (`P958-CONSUMED-RESEND-REFUSED`), because a DENY
would complete the sender's next pending entry on that resource with the old
one's error.  `acq_seq` is strictly increasing per requester, so a fresh
acquisition never collides with a tombstone.  Test-only knobs:
`dl_stale_resend_ino` (the sender keeps its last LOCK_REQ for that inode and
re-sends it once right after its next LOCK_RELEASE of it,
`P958-STALE-RESEND-SENT`, counter `dl_stale_resend_n` reset on write) and
`dl_no_consumed_tomb` (the master ignores the ring: the control arm).

Measured (2 nodes / TCP, 0.84.13 sv C91D38D944002747AD51092):

- s596a `tests/tcp_stale_resend.sh` (tests/evidence/20260912T124848Z_staleresend_s596a,
  PASS fails=0, 51 s): W's stale copy went out once after its release
  (`acq_done=1`), the master refused it by name (1 `P958-CONSUMED-RESEND-REFUSED`
  for the target), no phantom grant reached W (0 bounces), W's next read
  returned H's bytes.
- s596b the same lap with `CONTROL=1` (tests/evidence/20260912T124941Z_staleresend_s596b,
  PASS fails=0, 51 s): with the ring disabled on the master the same build
  reproduced the old shape — 0 refusals, the copy queued afresh and granted,
  1 `P958-ACQ-GRANT-BOUNCED` on W.
- s596c `tests/tcp_lockreq_blackhole.sh WORKLOAD=dir_lookup EXPECT=bounded
  ARMED_S=300` (tests/evidence/20260912T125034Z_lockreqbh_s596c, PASS
  fails=0, 435 s): with nothing re-cached after H's revoke, W's `os.stat` of
  an entry by path parked in the lookup's acquire, was reported DEGRADED at
  45 s, and was refused 185 s after the first dropped request
  (`P912-ACQ-UNRECEIPTED` then `P958-LOOKUP-REFUSED stage=refresh rc=-5`,
  `OSError: [Errno 5]`); 180 requests dropped, cancel acked ABSENT, no
  shutdown, W's fresh read after the disarm equal to H's.  The refusal met
  the refresh, which is the first of the two acquires; the `stage=dir` peek

  exercised by this shape.
- s596e `tests/live_holder_wait.sh RW=lookup TARGET=dir PAUSE_MS=240000`
  (tests/evidence/20260912T130445Z_livewait_s596e, PASS fails=0, 268 s): the

- s596f `tests/live_holder_wait.sh RW=dio_unaligned PAUSE_MS=240000`

Not measured: the fault arm for the unaligned retry

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.12 — unlink, link, rename and symlink take their first acquire as a fallible boundary; the namespace class is closed

D-0958, the remaining namespace operations.  Each takes its first cluster
acquire where its transaction is reserved and clean and nothing is joined,
and each now fails cleanly there instead of restarting the wait for ever:

- `xfs_remove` and `xfs_link` acquire the directory and the child as a pair
  inside `xfs_trans_alloc_dir` (`xfs/xfs_trans.c`).  The pair goes through
  `mxfs_lock_two_inodes_fallible`, which registers BOTH inodes for the
  duration of `xfs_lock_two_inodes` (its ordering, ABBA breaker and rwsem
  retry loops run unchanged); a refused member releases the pair and the
  helper cancels the reservation, so the caller returns the errno through
  the same path a failed reservation takes.
- `xfs_rename` acquires two to five inodes in `xfs_lock_inodes`; the set goes
  through `mxfs_lock_inodes_fallible` the same way, and a refusal cancels
  the still-clean transaction through the path a failed dquot attach already
  takes (the whiteout's own committed allocation is unwound by
  `out_release_wip` exactly as for any failure after it).
- `xfs_symlink` (`pal/linux/xfs_symlink.c`) takes the parent exactly as
  `xfs_create` does since 0.84.11.

Every refusal names its operation (`P958-NAMESPACE-REFUSED
op=remove|link|rename|symlink`, `xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c`).  A refused member of a
set does not stop the other members' acquires — they wait as before — so a
refusal costs at most one budget per faulted member; in the measured shape
the directory is the lower inode number and goes first.  No dirty
transaction is ever cancelled.

Measured (2 nodes / TCP, 0.84.12 sv 1FD01072ED6DC8C7B628024), the fault
arm `tests/tcp_lockreq_blackhole.sh WORKLOAD=<op> EXPECT=bounded ARMED_S=300`
— W re-caches the directory's PR, the positive lookup of the entry it reads
and the negative lookup of the name it would write, then issues the one
syscall through python's os.<op>; the drop instrument fires 180 times; the
op parks in its own acquire (`__x64_sys_unlink|rename|link|symlink ->
mxfs_dlm_lock_retries`, no `xfs_lookup`), is reported DEGRADED at 45 s and
refused between 243 s and 310 s of the window with `OSError: [Errno 5]`;
after the disarm the master answered the cancel ABSENT, the existing entry
exists on BOTH nodes, the new name on NEITHER (cold lookups), no shutdown,
no dirty cancel:

- s595d unlink (tests/evidence/20260912T114602Z_lockreqbh_s595d, PASS
  fails=0, 494 s): `op=remove`.
- s595e rename (tests/evidence/20260912T115421Z_lockreqbh_s595e, PASS
  fails=0, 446 s): `op=rename`.
- s595f link (tests/evidence/20260912T120226Z_lockreqbh_s595f, PASS fails=0,
  454 s): `op=link`.
- s595g symlink (tests/evidence/20260912T121010Z_lockreqbh_s595g, PASS
  fails=0, 444 s): `op=symlink`, refused in `xfs_ilock_fallible` under
  `__x64_sys_symlink`.

and the control `tests/live_holder_wait.sh RW=<op> TARGET=dir
PAUSE_MS=240000` — the op behind H's 240 s paused EX on the directory waited
243-244 s receipted (`P-LKWAIT-LIVE`, 233-234 re-sends, 11 absorbed by the
master, never DEGRADED), landed after H's pause end on H's clock, and H's

- s595h unlink (tests/evidence/20260912T121743Z_livewait_s595h, PASS fails=0,

- s595i rename (tests/evidence/20260912T122222Z_livewait_s595i, PASS fails=0,

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.11 — A create's first acquire of its parent directory is a fallible boundary that cancels a clean reservation

D-0958's next site, in the ruling's order: a namespace operation that has
only RESERVED a transaction.  `xfs_create` (which also serves mkdir) reserves
log space and quota in `xfs_trans_alloc_icreate` and then takes the parent's
`XFS_ILOCK_EXCL | XFS_ILOCK_PARENT` — the directory's cluster EX — before
`xfs_dialloc` allocates anything.  At that acquire nothing is dirty, no
inode exists, nothing is joined, and the pre-lock directory reload takes no
lock; the quarantine backstop already cancelled the reservation from that
point.  The acquire now goes through `mxfs_ilock_fallible`: when the grant
under it is abandoned (a live master never acknowledged the request past
the budget, or the task was killed) the create cancels the clean
transaction through the ordinary `out_trans_cancel` unwind and fails the
syscall with the refusal's errno holding nothing (`P958-NAMESPACE-REFUSED
op=create|mkdir`, `xfs/xfs_inode.c`; the helper in `xfs_mxfs_dlm.c`).  No
dirty transaction is ever cancelled: the boundary is before the first
mutation, which is the ruling's condition for a namespace op to be fallible.

Measured (2 nodes / TCP, 0.84.11 sv 340A625F5106AE63D530582):

- s595a, `tests/tcp_lockreq_blackhole.sh WORKLOAD=dir_create EXPECT=bounded
  ARMED_S=300` (tests/evidence/20260912T111701Z_lockreqbh_s595a, PASS
  fails=0, wall 495 s): W re-cached the directory's PR and the negative
  lookup of the name, then its `os.open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL)` parked in the
  create's own acquire (stack `do_sys_openat2 -> lookup_open -> xfs_create ->
  mxfs_ilock_fallible`, no `xfs_lookup`), was reported DEGRADED 45 s after
  the first dropped request, refused between 243 s and 310 s of the window
  (`P912-ACQ-UNRECEIPTED`, `P958-NAMESPACE-REFUSED op=create` for the
  directory, `OSError: [Errno 5] Input/output error`, 180 requests dropped,
  no fd returned), and cancelled CLEAN: `P-CR3-CANCEL error=-5 dp_ino=40887
  dialloc_ino=0 new_ino=0 trans_dirty=0`.  No shutdown, no
  'Corruption of in-memory data'; the master answered the cancel ABSENT;
  after the disarm the name existed on neither node (cold lookup on both),
  W's fresh listing matched H's, and the DEGRADED entry was retracted.
- s595c, `tests/live_holder_wait.sh RW=create TARGET=dir PAUSE_MS=240000`
  (the control, tests/evidence/20260912T113002Z_livewait_s595c, PASS
  fails=0, wall 266 s): W's create in a directory H held in EX with its
  release paused waited 242 s (`P-LKWAIT-LIVE` at the budget, 232 re-sends,
  receipted throughout, never DEGRADED), landed after H's pause end on H's
  clock (`create_fd=3 create_rc=0`), and H's cold listing of the directory
  equals W's and contains the name; zero `P958-NAMESPACE-REFUSED`, zero
  shutdowns, 26 blocking notifications against a budget of 29.

One harness lesson from the control's first attempt (s595b, aborted at
setup): a directory holder that still caches PR after the probe listing
takes its own PR-to-EX upgrade through the self-demote release drain, so a
release pause armed BEFORE the holder's re-dirty parks the holder itself for
the whole pause.  For `TARGET=dir` the harness now re-dirties first and arms
second; the file order is unchanged and the comment at that step says why.

The record stays open for unlink, link, rename, symlink (their first
acquires sit inside `xfs_trans_alloc_dir` and `xfs_lock_inodes`, two inodes
at once), the unaligned-DIO and atomic-write retries, writeback,
inactivation and every transactional acquire.

Harness additions: `tests/tcp_lockreq_blackhole.sh` gained
`WORKLOAD=dir_create`; `tests/live_holder_wait.sh` gained `RW=create` with
`TARGET=dir`; the budget rows in `tests/criteria/TIMEOUT_BUDGETS.md` cover
both.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.10 — The write path's first IOLOCK ride is a fallible acquire; a real transport fault is measured self-healing

D-0958's remaining class is every caller that cannot be failed waiting
without bound on an acquire a live master never acknowledged.  Before
touching it, the fault the record had only ever imitated with the per-inode
request drop was produced for real: 60 s into a receipted wait behind H's
paused release, W black-holed its DLM link to H (iptables, port 7600 both
ways, lease multicast and disk heartbeat untouched) for 27 s
(`tests/live_holder_wait.sh TCP_FAULT_S=25`, s594c,
tests/evidence/20260912T103221Z_livewait_s594c).  Both nodes logged the
disconnect 26 s in and deferred death for 40 s, reconnected 1.4 s after the
rules lifted and cancelled the pending death; the master absorbed W's
re-sends by acquisition id across the reconnect (`P958-ACQ-RETX retx=64
requeued_total=0`), the wait stayed receipted, and W's read returned H's
bytes at 246 s after H's pause end, with no death, no fence and no shutdown.
A socket-level fault shorter than the grace is therefore bounded by the
transport's own detection, reconnect and the 1 s re-send loop; the repair
worker the ruling sketched is not what the remaining class needs.  What
remains unbounded is a request discarded at message level on a healthy
socket, which the ruling says closes only by widening the fallible class
site by site — so the write path is now audited and converted.

`xfs_ilock_iocb_write` (`pal/linux/xfs_file.c`) takes the buffered, DAX and
aligned / atomic / unaligned direct writers' first ride, the relock for
security-attribute removal and the exclusive re-take before EOF zeroing
through `mxfs_ilock_fallible`: at each of them nothing has been copied,
dirtied, allocated or submitted, and the ordinary error return unwinds them.
A refused ride fails the write with -EIO holding nothing and says so
(`P958-WRITE-REFUSED stage=`).  IOCB_NOWAIT never enters the wait.  Not
converted, deliberately: the exclusive retry of an unaligned direct write
after -EAGAIN and the COW retry of an atomic write, both of which re-acquire
behind an attempt that may have submitted part of the range and would
otherwise report a partly landed write as an error.

Measured (2 nodes / TCP, 0.84.10 sv FF25B785E9F251FFCA95E38):

- s594d, `tests/tcp_lockreq_blackhole.sh WORKLOAD=held_fd_write EXPECT=bounded
  ARMED_S=300` (tests/evidence/20260912T104806Z_lockreqbh_s594d, PASS
  fails=0, wall 407 s): W's write(2) through an fd opened for append before
  the fault parked in the write path's own ride (stack `ksys_write ->
  mxfs_ilock_fallible -> mxfs_dlm_lock_retries`), was reported DEGRADED 45 s
  after the first dropped request, refused between 194 s and 259 s of the
  window (`P912-ACQ-UNRECEIPTED`, `P958-WRITE-REFUSED` for the target,
  `OSError: [Errno 5] Input/output error` to userspace, 180 requests dropped,
  no bytes moved), no shutdown; after the disarm the process was gone in 5 s,
  the DEGRADED entry retracted, and a fresh read returned H's bytes.
- s594e, `tests/live_holder_wait.sh RW=write PAUSE_MS=240000` (the control,
  tests/evidence/20260912T105553Z_livewait_s594e, PASS fails=0): W's append
  behind H's 240 s paused release waited 243 s (`P-LKWAIT-LIVE` at the budget,
  233 re-sends, receipted throughout), landed 4096 bytes after H's pause end
  on H's clock, and H's fresh read of the file equals W's digest; zero
  `P958-WRITE-REFUSED`, zero shutdowns.

The record stays open for the namespace operations, writeback, inactivation
and every transactional acquire; its next step is the first acquire of the
namespace operations that have only reserved a transaction.  Also recorded on
it: during s594c's candidate probes a re-send in flight at grant time was
processed after W's release as a fresh request and granted again, which W
bounced (`P958-ACQ-GRANT-BOUNCED`, harmless as measured, the duplicate-
pending-after-release gap the ruling names).

Harness additions: `tests/live_holder_wait.sh` gained `TCP_FAULT_S` /
`TCP_FAULT_AT_S` (the timed black-hole) and `RW=write`;
`tests/tcp_lockreq_blackhole.sh` gained `WORKLOAD=held_fd_write`; the budget
rows in `tests/criteria/TIMEOUT_BUDGETS.md` cover all three.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.9 — Foreign replay of a released tenure's image is measured REDUNDANT_CLEAN, never applied; D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-UNGATED-IMAGES disposed

The record was filed against 0.11.x, when a dead node's buffer images were
replayed behind nothing but upstream's on-disk-LSN compare — meaningless
across per-node slices, so an older image of a block the survivor had since
rewritten could be applied over it (false-APPLY) and a held image could be
dropped (false-SKIP).  The gate the record's ruling asked for has shipped
since: every buffer and icreate image carries a v3 authority token
{class, resource, lineage, grant epoch, owner slot, owner incarnation},
`foreign_replay_token_enforce` defaults to 1 (0.54.0), the verdict comes from
the sealed fence-time manifest (held with the same lineage and epoch → APPLY)
or from the victim's own clean-release marker, forced durable before its
unlock CAS (→ REDUNDANT_CLEAN, skipped), and anything else refuses the whole
transaction closed.  What had never been measured on the ship shape was the
REDUNDANT_CLEAN verdict on a real image: a released tenure's image is landed
by the release drain and the destage kick empties the AIL within
milliseconds, so the on-disk tail moves past it and the survivor's replay
window holds only the markers (s593h: txn=0 buf=0 relmarks=2).

A test-only knob makes that window deterministic: `mxfs.dbg_ail_pin_ino=<ino>`
(`xfs/xfs_inode_item.c`) keeps one inode item in the AIL — its push answers
LOCKED and `xfs_iflush_cluster` skips it (`P-AILPIN-HOLD`) — so the node's
log tail is pinned behind everything logged after it.  Never set it on a node
meant to survive.  `tests/tcp_death_replay.sh TDR_FALSE_APPLY=3` drives it:
the victim pins a file, logs six creates into the survivor's block-format
directory, is BASTed off it by the survivor's own four creates (drain, marker,
release) and is destroyed with the older images still inside its window.

Measured (2 nodes / TCP, 0.84.9 sv 5A0C7F40AB3136A0A450C99 and 0.84.8 sv
7166251E2633D79F04B48B7):

- s594b (`TDR_FALSE_APPLY=3`, tests/evidence/20260912T102244Z_tcpdr_s594b,
  RESULT PASS fails=0): the pin engaged on the victim (`P-AILPIN-HOLD n=4`
  before the kill); the survivor's window held 16 transactions and 66 buffer
  images, `WOULD_APPLY=39 ENFORCEABLE_WOULD_APPLY=39 REDUNDANT_CLEAN=27
  redundant_skipped=27 relmarks=3 notheld=0 staleep=0 wlineage=0 untagged=0`,
  27 `P227-FR-REDUNDANT-SKIP` lines and zero `P227-FR-ATOMIC-SKIP`; the
  survivor's four names and all 13 of the victim's acknowledged files read
  with their md5 at verdict time, after drop_caches=2, and cold after the
  survivor unmounted and remounted alone (17/17).  The released images were
  in front of the replayer and were not applied.
- s594a (`TDR_FALSE_APPLY=2`, re-hold: the victim re-takes the directory after
  the survivor's adds, logs a new image under a new grant epoch and dies
  holding it; 20260912T101047Z_tcpdr_s594a): `buf=7 WOULD_APPLY=7
  REDUNDANT_CLEAN=0 relmarks=1 notheld=0 staleep=0`, 18/18 files including
  both nodes' names cold.  The lap's three failing lines are the gate
  restore waiting on the D-0962 takeover pace (below), not the replay.
- s593g (victim killed mid-stream holding its grants,
  20260912T094158Z_tcpdr_s593g): `buf=18 WOULD_APPLY=18` applied, 715/715
  acknowledged files cold — the held-at-death direction (no false-SKIP).
- s593h (`TDR_FALSE_APPLY=1`, 20260912T095057Z_tcpdr_s593h): window of
  markers only, 17/17 cold; the lap that showed the window had to be pinned.

Disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED on 2/tcp — the mechanism the record names no
longer exists in the untrusted replay path for any transport, and both
directions were exercised on the ship shape.  CAW was not run (scope
decision of 2026-09-05).  The record is removed from the queue.

Also this version:

- D-0962 re-read from the survivor's live log: recovery-complete and the
  exclusive-write gate restore are not lost, they wait on the sequential
  takeover of every ledger page the victim owned inside the completion —
  `P-COMPLETE-TIMING handoff_ms=103767` for 7984 pages (s594a, completion
  104.5 s after the replay), 107376 (s593g), 43373 (s593h), 52981 for 4663
  pages (s594b): ~11-13 ms per page, each an auth read, prepare, activate,
  purge and import against the ledger.  The late TCP-transport death event
  the record blamed appears in every lap, passing ones included.  The record
  now says so and asks for the batched takeover; the harness prints the page
  count and the timing line when its 60 s restore wait runs out.
- `tests/criteria/TIMEOUT_BUDGETS.md`: the released-tenure row covers the
  =3 arm and carries the s593h/s594a walls.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.8 — A joiner is held at the settle gate until the incumbent's beacon carries the two-node view

The settle gate (0.83.4) was fail-closed only against a live member whose
beacon reports a *different* view.  An incumbent that has not finished its
join prepare beacons the view `{0, 0}` — no multi-node view installed, which
for the joiner means "not admitted yet" — and that report was dropped twice
on the way in: the lease receiver forwarded only a non-zero hash, and
`mxfs_dlm_report_peer_view` returned on hash 0.  With no report to weigh
against the wall clock the gate opened unconfirmed at the 20 s window
(`P-D7-SETTLEGATE waited=18000ms confirmed=0`), and every cluster acquire the
joiner then made met the incumbent's page-handoff handler under a view
mismatch and was answered DEFER every 500 ms.  A DEFER carries no progress
and is a plain park, so the joiner's retry budget went on it — nine
60-retry budgets of `prepare=60` and the untrusted iget's five, then
`Failed to read root inode ... error 5` (s592e, the root's page mastered by
the joiner) — or the transition watchdog fired with the relayed count
frozen (s593a, `P960-AUTH-TRANSITION-STALLED progress=2463 stalled_ms=30029`,
the root's page mastered by the joiner while AG 0's was the incumbent's).
Both were clean refusals — no shutdown, no withdraw, no fence, defence C of
0.84.5 held — but the join failed while the cluster was healthy, inside the
window D-0960 is about: the incumbent's prepare took 55 s behind its own
ledger takeover.

A zero view signature is now forwarded and recorded like any other, so an
incumbent beaconing it since the joiner's membership change is a live member
reporting another view: `dlm_view_pending_live` says so, the gate stays
closed past the window, and it opens on the incumbent's installed view — the
positive proof — rather than on the clock.  The 60 s backstop still refuses
the acquire (retryable; the mount's untrusted iget retries it up to five
budgets), so an incumbent whose prepare never completes ends in a refused
mount, never a hang.  `P-D7-SETTLEGATE` prints `pending_live=`.  The DEFER
path is unchanged: it is the safety net behind the gate, not a wait.

Measured (2 nodes / TCP, 0.84.8 sv 7166251E2633D79F04B48B7,
`tests/join_during_takeover.sh EXPECT=clean`, B joining inside A's ~16k-page
takeover of its own previous incarnation):

- `ARM=ondemand` (production, s593c, tests/evidence/20260912T083241Z_jointk_s593c,
  and six more iterations in s593e, 20260912T085752Z_jointk_s593e): B's
  mount inside the pass returned 0 every time — 3.0 s, then 13.2, 2.9,
  13.4, 13.2, 13.2, 13.2 s — with A serving three pages on demand each
  time, the root's or AG 0's at its own prepare and one by takeover-request
  for a page B masters; no settle-gate wait at all (A installed the
  two-node view before B's first acquire); no REMASTER, no budget, no
  DEFER; both nodes read the 32000 entries after every lap.  s593c fails=0;
  s593e's one FAIL is the harness asking for the root request itself to
  land on a page B masters, which it did not in six flips — its A-shape
  test takes precedence whenever AG 0's page is A's.
- `ARM=nodemand` (on-demand service off on A, s593b,
  tests/evidence/20260912T080602Z_jointk_s593b, two iterations): A's install
  waited on the pass for its SB summary lock's page
  (`P960-AUTH-TRANSITION-WAIT comm=mxfs-worker`, `P-JOIN-INSTALLED ms=214185`),
  the gate held B's AG 0 acquire on `pending_live=1` — refused three times at
  the 60 s backstop, retried by the untrusted iget, opened on
  `confirmed=1` at 212 s — and B's mount returned 0 in 219.7 s and 214.8 s
  inside the 700 s bound, with zero DEFER answers on A, zero retry budgets,
  no REMASTER, no stall, no shutdown, withdraw or fence; both nodes read the
  32000 entries afterwards (A 226 ms, B 411 ms).  The lap was stopped by hand
  after its second iteration before it printed a verdict; the figures are in
  its log.  The scored lap s593f (20260912T093117Z_jointk_s593f, one
  iteration, the root's page mastered by B): join in 221.2 s, gate refused
  three times then `confirmed=1`, A's worker waited on the pass by name and
  never stalled, zero DEFER, zero budgets, fails=0, wall 510 s.
- `ARM=stall` (on-demand off and the pass held 45 s a page, s593d,
  tests/evidence/20260912T083740Z_jointk_s593d): A's install never came (its
  worker's wait on the paused pass was named thirteen times and never failed
  it), the gate refused B's AG 0 acquire at its backstop ten times — the
  untrusted iget's five budgets, each a refusal of the non-blocking probe
  and one of the blocking acquire — and the mount was refused at the root
  lookup 628 s after it was issued, its command back inside the same 3 s
  poll, its quiesce writing no SB summary and taking no cluster lock,
  nothing half-mounted, no third-member view on A; once the knobs were
  cleared the pass finished (18335 pages, 899 s with the pause) and the same

- The same arm on 0.84.7 (s592e, s593a): the mount refused after 77 s and

No shutdown, withdraw, poison, fence, crash or budget exhaustion on either
node in any lap; D-0960 closed FIXED AND VERIFIED (the record's own
disposition text is in the queue tool's removal, this entry carries the
measurements).

Instrumentation kept: `P960-PARK-NOT-TRANSITION`, `P960-PARK-NOT-OWNER` and
`P960-PARK-IMPORT-STALE` name the three silent parks a retry budget can be
spent on.  `tests/join_during_takeover.sh` scopes every A-side count to a
marker written before A's remount (the previous lap's pass was still running
during step 1 and had been counted), records the gate's line and the
incumbent worker's wait, and scores the gate-admitted join as its own shape.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.7 — The join install's dead-set check and its lease registration are one critical section

0.84.6 made the join worker ask the dead set before installing a sighted
peer, but the check and the lease registration ran unlocked, while the
GOODBYE receiver's unregister-and-retire runs under the member lock: a
departure landing between the two would still have installed the departed
identity, and a view carrying one hangs both nodes at the settle gate for
ever (D-0961).  `v5_join_install` now takes the member lock around the check
and the registration, the same lock and the same order (member lock, then
the lease lock) the GOODBYE path uses, so the two claimants of a peer's
membership are ordered rather than raced.

`tests/join_during_takeover.sh` builds its 32000-entry authority while BOTH
nodes are members, before B leaves.  The ledger records grants; a lone mount
modifies everything at NL with no grant and writes no record, so on a fresh
filesystem the directory it created after B had left gave the takeover pass
4 candidate pages and 2.3 s of work (s591d, s592a), and the join could not
be issued inside it.  A stat of every entry under two members takes each
inode's grant at its master (P-TAUTH-PREPARED/ACTIVATE per inode, ~10 ms),
and B's clean departure hands B's pages to A.

Measured (2 nodes / TCP, `tests/join_during_takeover.sh EXPECT=clean`): the
stall arm — B's mount refused inside A's blocked prepare, B leaves, A's
prepare completes after — on 0.84.6 (s592b, two iterations, A-mastered then
B-mastered) and on 0.84.7 (s592c, B-mastered): A logged the departed
incarnation's sighting retired before and after the prepare, installed no
three-member view, and B's next mount returned in 3-7 s; the refusal itself
was logged 53-76 s after the mount was issued and the refused command
returned 1 s later.  The on-demand arm on 0.84.7 (s592d): the join inside an
18.5k-page pass returned in 13 s, three pages served on demand, no REMASTER
answer.  No shutdown, withdraw, fence, crash or budget exhaustion on either
node in any lap; D-0961 closed FIXED AND VERIFIED.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.6 — A peer that left while the incumbent was still preparing its join is no longer installed into the view

The single-to-multi join runs on a worker: the incumbent freezes its mount,
writes its dirty state back and drops its cached views (the D-0959 prepare),
and only then registers the sighted peer and installs the two-node view.  The
prepare can take a long time — its quiesce takes the SB summary cluster lock,
and behind a stalled authority transition that was 55 s (s591a) — and a peer
that mounts and leaves inside it (a mount refused for any reason, an
immediate unmount) has its GOODBYE processed, is noted as a retired identity,
and was then installed anyway: `v5_join_install` asked only whether the lease
already had the id, not whether the id was dead.  The incumbent's view then
carried a departed identity that no lease expiry retires (its heartbeat slot
beats under the peer's next incarnation), the peer's next mount saw a
two-member view against the incumbent's three, and every EX acquire on both
nodes was refused by the settle gate for ever ("a live member still reports
another view"): the mount never returned and the incumbent's own path
lookups blocked in the DLM retry loop (D-0961, measured 2 nodes / TCP on
0.84.5 sv B96EA6B773601B3A706BA88, tests/evidence/20260912T061256Z_jointk_s591a).

The join worker now asks the dead set before each prepare attempt and again
after a prepare succeeds, and the install itself refuses a retired identity:
`P961-JOIN-SIGHTING-RETIRED node= peer= at=before-prepare|after-prepare|install`,
the sighting is dropped, the frozen mount is thawed as before (join commit),
and no view names the departed peer.  The connect and announce paths already
made this check (`P164-DEAD-REJECT`); the install was the one membership
entry point that did not.  `tests/join_during_takeover.sh`'s stall arm now
asserts that the incumbent installed no three-member view and reads the main
pass's summary rather than the 50-page takeover of the refused mount's own
departed incarnation.

## 2026-09-12 — 0.84.5 — A node joining while the bootstrap node takes over a dead authority's ledger pages is served, waits on progress, or is refused — never shut down

A node that leaves a cluster as its last member keeps every ledger page it
served under its own authority.  When it mounts again, alone, its departure
worker runs the takeover-only pass over that incarnation's pages (~15k pages,
~10 ms each, 157 s on this LUN), and a node that joins inside that pass makes
its first cluster acquires — AG 0's lock for the untrusted root lookup, then
the root inode's EX — on pages the pass has not reached.  Measured (D-0960,
s588b/c and a plain `scripts/module_swap_deploy.sh`): the bootstrap's
on-demand takeover asked its node-id-keyed purged list, which can never name
its OWN previous incarnation, so the joiner's request was answered REMASTER
until the pass reached the page; sixty retries took 6 s, three descents 18 s,
the acquire classifier shut the joiner's filesystem down at mount, the mount
